title: Subthreshold SRAM sensing against accumulated column leakage
open: Reliably distinguish selected-cell current from accumulated leakage in long SRAM columns at subthreshold voltage. Demonstrate measured read-error tails across data patterns, temperature, and process variation without prohibitive sensing latency.
status: A constraint since the 2000s; Ultra8T's 2024 post-layout simulations read a 256×64 array at 0.25 V with 1.11 μs delay. Large-array silicon qualification remains distinct.
why: Memory leakage can set the minimum supply of an otherwise efficient processor.
key_works: Shan Shen et al. (2024 revision), [*Ultra8T: A Sub-Threshold 8T SRAM with Leakage Detection*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08936).

title: Measured temporal failure-tail laws for subthreshold SRAM
open: Predict full retention-failure distributions when process mismatch, non-Gaussian trap switching, and time-dependent noise interact in SRAM. Validate extreme tails against silicon arrays over independently chosen voltages and temperatures.
status: Investigated since the 2000s; a 2025 nonlinear stochastic model predicts mean failure times using an extended Eyring–Kramers formula. Experimentally transferable distribution tails remain a stronger target.
why: Static noise margins alone cannot certify long retention at very low voltage.
key_works: Léopold Van Brandt et al. (2025), [*Modeling and Predicting Noise-Induced Failure Rates in Ultra-Low-Voltage SRAM Bitcells Affected by Process Variations*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSI.2024.3525387).

title: Cryogenic SRAM read–write voltage asymmetry
open: Reduce the write-voltage floor of dense cryogenic SRAM while retaining its improved read stability. Demonstrate a common low-voltage operating window across array populations, cooldown cycles, and peripheral circuits.
status: Prominent during the 2010s–2020s; measured-device-calibrated 5-nm simulations in 2025 reported cryogenic read and write limits of 0.15 V and 0.45 V without assists.
why: Memory write voltage can dominate cryogenic control-system heat dissipation.
key_works: Hafeez Raza et al. (2025), [*An Investigation of Minimum Supply Voltage of 5-nm SRAM From 300 K Down to 10 K*](https://doi.org/10.1109/JXCDC.2025.3560215).

title: Manufacturable sub-0.01-square-micrometre CFET SRAM
open: Fabricate CFET SRAM below 0.01 μm² per bitcell with usable read/write margins, routable arrays, and demonstrated statistical yield. Include local interconnect resistance and transistor mismatch in measured macro performance.
status: A 2020s scaling target; Abdi's 2025 design–technology study predicts sub-0.01 μm² cells and improved write margins using wordline folding, rather than demonstrating a manufactured memory array.
why: SRAM area scaling increasingly constrains cache capacity and processor cost.
key_works: Dawit B. Abdi et al. (2025), [*SRAM Scaling Opportunities Below 0.01 μm² Using Double-Row CFET Architecture with Wordline-Folded Bitcell Design for Performance Optimization*](https://www.vlsisymposium.org/wp-content/uploads/VLSI2025_Advanceprogram0418.pdf).

title: Reliable sub-0.3-nanometre-EOT DRAM dielectrics
open: Achieve sub-0.3-nm equivalent oxide thickness in manufacturable three-dimensional DRAM capacitors while preserving low leakage and dielectric lifetime. Retain the benefit within electrode-thickness and thermal-budget limits.
status: Pursued for decades; 2024 rutile-TiO₂ capacitors reached 0.4-nm EOT. A 2026 assessment still identifies simultaneous phase stabilization, leakage control, and reliability as barriers.
why: Higher capacitance density can prevent further increases in capacitor height.
key_works: Jihoon Jeon et al. (2024), [*High-Temperature Atomic Layer Deposition of Rutile TiO₂ Films on RuO₂ Substrates: Interfacial Reactions and Dielectric Performance*](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.3c03324); Jeon et al. (2026), [*Beyond ZrO₂: Rutile TiO₂ as the Dielectric Platform for Next-Generation DRAM Capacitors*](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsaelm.5c02598).

title: Chemically stable ultrathin DRAM storage-node electrodes
open: Preserve electrode conductivity, mechanical integrity, and dielectric interface quality as storage-node electrodes and passivation layers become thinner. Prevent oxidation and interfacial reactions throughout capacitor fabrication and operation.
status: A long-standing scaling constraint; Kang's 2024 experiments improved MoNₓ electrodes using 2.5–14-nm TiN passivation. Maintaining protection under tighter total-thickness budgets remains open.
why: Electrode improvements are unusable if protective layers consume the available capacitor footprint.
key_works: Wangu Kang et al. (2024), [*Enhanced Oxidation Resistance and Interface Stability of Atomic-Layer-Deposited MoNₓ Electrodes via TiN Passivation for DRAM Cell Capacitor Applications*](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsami.4c14077).

title: Floating-body retention margins in silicon 3D DRAM
open: Bound transient bipolar leakage in body-contact-free silicon DRAM access transistors under realistic precharge and access histories. Demonstrate retention margins across full array distributions and temperature, beyond quasi-static off-current specifications.
status: A 2020s 3D-DRAM problem; Garbin's 2025 experiments isolated floating-body current in nanosheet arrays. Extrapolation predicts suppression at target leakage, leaving direct qualification across operating histories.
why: Dynamic body charging can discharge a storage capacitor faster than static tests predict.
key_works: Daniele Garbin et al. (2025), [*First Systematic Characterization of Floating Body Effects in GAA Nanosheet 3D DRAM Access Transistors*](https://doi.org/10.1109/IEDM50572.2025.11353614).

title: Charge-sharing-resistant advanced-node storage latches
open: Preserve latch data after multi-node charge collection from high-LET particle strikes while keeping practical area, delay, and power. Validate protection across strike angles, voltage, temperature, and realistic physical layouts.
status: Charge sharing has challenged scaling for decades; 2025 heavy-ion tests of 14-nm FinFET flip-flops found interleaved redundancy effective, while conventional DICE protection degraded at high LET.
why: Nominal logical redundancy need not survive physically correlated disturbances.
key_works: Hai-song Li et al. (2025), [*Investigation of DFF cells SEU effect for 14 nm bulk silicon FinFET technology irradiated by heavy ions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115857).

title: Low-capacitance ESD protection within scaled-device failure windows
open: Clamp fast discharge transients below protected-device damage thresholds while maintaining low I/O capacitance and adequate discharge current. Establish scalable structures that avoid local thermal failure at advanced FinFET dimensions.
status: A decades-old narrowing-window problem; 2025 simulations of 5-nm diodes found different geometries best for breakdown current and capacitance. Their simultaneous optimization remains unresolved.
why: Protection devices can otherwise constrain signal bandwidth or fail before protecting logic.
key_works: Dae-Yeol You, Jaeho Lee and Kang-Il Cho (2025), [*Design considerations for ESD protection diodes in bulk FinFET technology*](https://doi.org/10.1587/elex.22.20240755).

title: Stable probability calibration across stochastic-MTJ populations
open: Maintain reproducible probability-versus-input curves and useful fluctuation times across large stochastic-MTJ populations despite process variation, temperature, and ageing. Bound the energy and area required for calibration and its refresh.
status: A 2010s–2020s problem; on-chip p-bit cores appeared in 2024, and 2025 delay-based circuits compensated offsets and demonstrated five-device sampling. Population-wide lifetime stability remains unestablished.
why: Biased physical random variables can corrupt inference even when digital logic is correct.
key_works: John Daniel et al. (2024), [*Experimental demonstration of an on-chip p-bit core based on stochastic magnetic tunnel junctions and 2D MoS₂ transistors*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-48152-0); Kemal Selcuk et al. (2025), [*DAC-Free p-bits: Asynchronous Self-Coloring and On-Chip Annealing*](https://doi.org/10.1109/IEDM50572.2025.11353558).

title: Faithful sampling in physically coupled stochastic-MTJ networks
open: Bound stationary-distribution errors when physical p-bit coupling delays compete with heterogeneous magnetic fluctuation times. Demonstrate faithful sampling in programmable frustrated networks with realistic sensing and interconnect overhead.
status: A 2010s–2020s challenge; 2024 experiments coupled two stochastic MTJs programmably. Million-p-bit FPGA sampling appeared in 2026, but does not establish equivalent physical-MTJ network dynamics.
why: More stochastic devices provide useful acceleration only if their collective dynamics sample the intended distribution.
key_works: Sidra Gibeault et al. (2024), [*Programmable electrical coupling between stochastic magnetic tunnel junctions*](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevApplied.21.034064); Navid Anjum Aadit et al. (2026 preprint), [*Programmable Probabilistic Computer with 1,000,000 p-bits*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25313).

title: NEM relay contacts with stable loaded-switching lifetimes
open: Develop relay contacts retaining low resistance and repeatable release through prolonged switching of realistic capacitive loads. Quantify and suppress the competing effects of adhesion, wear, oxidation, and microwelding at small contact forces.
status: Central since 2000s NEM logic proposals; 2026 shock/vibration tests preserved mechanical function but found contact-related electrical variability and gold-coating wear. Mechanical survival alone does not establish switching lifetime.
why: Contact degradation can defeat the energy advantage of essentially zero off-state leakage.
key_works: Ivan Marozau et al. (2026), [*Mechanical shock and vibration testing of volatile and non-volatile nanoelectromechanical switches*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.microrel.2025.115980).

title: Fatal-defect tails in EUV lithography
open: Predict missing contacts, bridges, and broken lines at product-relevant rare-event probabilities from resist chemistry and exposure conditions, with calibrated uncertainty rather than extrapolation from average roughness.
status: Explicitly studied since the 2010s; De Bisschop quantified stochastic failures in 2018, while 2026 high-NA development still identifies stochastic defects as a yield barrier.
why: Makes defect-limited yield predictable before expensive product wafers.
key_works: De Bisschop (2018), [“Stochastic printing failures in extreme ultraviolet lithography”](https://doi.org/10.1117/1.JMM.17.4.041011).

title: Tight dose–resolution–defectivity bounds
open: Establish achievable lower bounds on exposure dose for specified pitch and fatal-defect probability, separating unavoidable photon statistics from improvable chemical randomness.
status: A longstanding resist trade-off; De Silva and colleagues experimentally separated material and dose effects in 2019. A universal, chemistry-aware bound remains a research target.
why: Distinguishes fundamental throughput limits from opportunities for better resists.
key_works: De Silva et al. (2019), [“Fundamentals of resist stochastics effect for single-expose EUV patterning”](https://research.ibm.com/publications/fundamentals-of-resist-stochastics-effect-for-single-expose-euv-patterning).

title: Thin high-NA resist with reliable pattern transfer
open: Transfer the smallest high-NA resist features into functional materials without collapse, excessive roughness, or unacceptable defect density, using films thin enough for the available depth of focus.
status: Metal-oxide and vapor-deposited resists provide substantial partial progress; the combined thickness, sensitivity, and etch-durability problem remains explicit in a 2026 review.
why: Converts optical resolution into usable transistor and interconnect density.
key_works: Chu et al. (2026), [“Recent efforts of vapour-phase strategies for EUV resist toward high- and hyper-NA extreme ultraviolet lithography”](https://doi.org/10.1039/D6SC02112C).

title: Direct measurement of the EUV latent chemical image
open: Measure exposure-induced chemical heterogeneity in three dimensions before development, then connect it quantitatively to the final defect map without significantly altering the resist.
status: A current NIST metrology program combines soft-X-ray measurements and in-situ development monitoring; routine causal reconstruction of individual failures remains the goal.
why: Reveals whether exposure, chemistry, or development created a defect.
key_works: NIST (2024–2026), [“Advanced Metrology to Enable Next Generation EUV Photoresists”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/advanced-metrology-enable-next-generation-euv-photoresists).

title: High-NA mask three-dimensional effects
open: Co-design mask absorbers, illumination, and proximity correction so that polarization and mask topography do not cause unacceptable orientation-dependent focus or placement errors across arbitrary product layouts.
status: High-NA ecosystem development has advanced beyond test patterns; anamorphic masks, resist, and imaging still require joint optimization in the 2026 imec assessment.
why: Allows dense two-dimensional logic patterns to use the scanner's resolution.
key_works: Vandenberghe (2026), [“The case for High NA EUV: unlocking the next era of chip manufacturing”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/case-high-na-euv-unlocking-next-era-chip-manufacturing).

title: Pellicles for sustained higher-power EUV
open: Preserve high EUV transmission and particle protection through prolonged radiation, hydrogen exposure, thermal cycling, and scanner acceleration at future source powers.
status: Since the 2010s, silicon and carbon-based membranes have improved; imec described CNT pellicles targeting powers beyond 600 W. Higher-power service life remains distinct from short survival demonstrations.
why: Prevents reticle contamination without sacrificing exposure throughput.
key_works: imec (2021), [“High-NA EUV lithography: the next step after EUVL”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/high-na-euvl-next-major-step-lithography).

title: Buried EUV-mask phase-defect inspection
open: Detect, localize, and assess the printability of buried multilayer mask defects at production throughput, including defects obscured by patterned absorbers or pellicles.
status: Nanoscale optical detection and phase-sensitive techniques have progressed for over a decade; a 2013 NIST study demonstrated useful defect discrimination, not exhaustive production inspection.
why: Avoids repeating one invisible mask defect across many wafers.
key_works: Attota and Jindal (2013), [“Through-focus scanning optical microscopy for defect inspection of EUV masks”](https://www.nist.gov/publications/through-focus-scanning-optical-microscopy-defect-inspection-euv-masks).

title: Yield-preserving high-NA field stitching
open: Join exposure fields for large dies while maintaining overlay, electrical continuity, and defect yield across the seam over production-scale wafer populations.
status: The smaller anamorphic field makes this a specific high-NA issue; imec's 2026 assessment still lists stitching enablement among remaining challenges.
why: Extends high-NA patterning to large accelerators and other reticle-limited designs.
key_works: Vandenberghe (2026), [“The case for High NA EUV: unlocking the next era of chip manufacturing”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/case-high-na-euv-unlocking-next-era-chip-manufacturing).

title: Tenfold lower EUV energy per yielding exposure
open: Proposed moonshot: reduce total electricity per good patterned wafer layer tenfold against a declared production baseline, holding pitch, defect yield, and throughput requirements fixed.
status: ASML demonstrated a 1,000 W EUV source in April 2025; its account distinguishes that milestone from a commercial source. Optical power alone does not establish energy per good wafer.
why: Reduces operating cost and the environmental burden of scaling.
key_works: ASML (2026), [“Strategy & stories,” 2025 Annual Report](https://www.asml.com/en/investors/annual-report/2025/strategy-and-stories).

title: Fast, defect-correcting directed self-assembly
open: Make block copolymers assemble the required irregular device patterns within manufacturing cycle times while reliably removing kinetically trapped dislocations and bridges.
status: Long studied; imec demonstrated 18 nm-pitch high-chi line/space patterning in 2021. Periodic pattern resolution does not settle arbitrary-layout defectivity and assembly kinetics.
why: Adds density multiplication and pattern smoothing without proportional exposure cost.
key_works: imec (2021), [“Imec Demonstrates 18nm Pitch Line/Space Patterning With a High-Chi Directed Self-Assembly Process”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/imec-demonstrates-18nm-pitch-linespace-patterning-high-chi-directed-self-assembly-process).

title: Nanoimprint overlay and defectivity at product scale
open: Demonstrate sustained competitive yield, overlay, template lifetime, and cost on multilayer leading-edge products, including particle events and template-to-template variation.
status: Nanoimprint equipment and nanometer-scale alignment already exist; commercial qualification and scaling of the combined requirements remain separate from feature-resolution demonstrations.
why: Could provide a lower-cost route to dense patterning.
key_works: Canon (2018; living page), [“Nanoimprint opens a new door to the future of digital society”](https://global.canon/en/business/group/industry/2018.html); Sreenivasan (2017), [“Nanoimprint lithography steppers for volume fabrication of leading-edge semiconductor integrated circuits”](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6445000/).

title: Economically useful patterning beyond 0.55 NA
open: Establish whether hyper-NA EUV or a shorter wavelength can deliver lower total patterning cost at required yield than 0.55-NA multiple patterning, including masks, sources, resist, and metrology.
status: Neisser's 2026 roadmap presentation describes hyper-NA as conditional on economics and shorter-wavelength options as lacking consensus or demonstrated feasibility.
why: Determines whether another optical generation can extend density scaling.
key_works: Neisser (2026), [“Lithography and Patterning,” IRDS/ISRDS workshop abstract](https://sinano.eu/irds-isrds-workshop-in-granada-registration-is-open/).

title: Area-selective deposition without rare unwanted nuclei
open: Grow useful film thickness selectively on realistic mixed surfaces while keeping unwanted nuclei below the product's killer-defect budget over whole wafers.
status: Selective ALD is established for selected combinations; Mackus and colleagues quantified how demanding defect-based selectivity becomes in 2019. Selectivity commonly erodes with cycle count.
why: Enables self-aligned fabrication with fewer patterning and overlay steps.
key_works: Mackus, Merkx, and Kessels (2019), [“From the Bottom-Up: Toward Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition with High Selectivity”](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b03454).

title: Predictive precursor–inhibitor design
open: Predict selective-deposition windows from molecular structure while accounting for surface defects, finite coverage, competing reactions, and temperature, then validate on previously untested material pairs.
status: Atomistic approaches now rationalize many individual reactions; a 2025 review identifies the remaining gap between tractable calculations and realistic selective growth.
why: Replaces repeated empirical screening of expensive process chemistries.
key_works: Pieck and Tonner-Zech (2025), [“Computational Ab Initio Approaches for Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition: Methods, Status, and Perspectives”](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c03477).

title: Damage-free selective atomic-layer etching
open: Remove a controlled atomic increment from one material in a heterogeneous stack without changing the composition, roughness, or electrical quality of neighboring exposed materials, at useful throughput.
status: ALE has decades of demonstrations and manufacturing uses; the 2015 overview and 2024 plasma roadmap retain selectivity, new-material coverage, and productivity challenges.
why: Preserves electrical interfaces as feature dimensions approach individual atomic layers.
key_works: Kanarik et al. (2015), [“Overview of atomic layer etching in the semiconductor industry”](https://doi.org/10.1116/1.4913379).

title: Extreme-aspect-ratio dielectric etch fidelity
open: Etch deeper oxide/nitride stacks without unacceptable bowing, twisting, taper, charging damage, or bottom-CD variation across different local pattern densities.
status: High-aspect-ratio etching and cryogenic methods have advanced substantially; the 2024 plasma-etch roadmap still identifies transport and profile control as scaling barriers.
why: Enables more stacked memory layers and taller three-dimensional structures.
key_works: Oehrlein et al. (2024), [“Future of plasma etching for microelectronics: Challenges and opportunities”](https://doi.org/10.1116/6.0003579).

title: Fast conformal deposition in deep closed-end features
open: Obtain uniform thickness and composition throughout increasingly deep structures without exposure and purge times that make deposition uneconomic.
status: ALD is already highly conformal; the unresolved scaling trade-off couples precursor transport, sticking, depletion, and radical recombination, systematized by Cremers and colleagues in 2019.
why: Supports reliable capacitors, memory channels, and three-dimensional gate stacks.
key_works: Cremers, Puurunen, and Dendooven (2019), [“Conformality in atomic layer deposition: Current status overview of analysis and modelling”](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5060967).

title: Transferable plasma-to-profile digital twins
open: Predict etched profiles and damage for new chambers, recipes, and materials using coupled plasma and surface models with validated uncertainty and limited calibration wafers.
status: Hybrid simulation and machine learning are active partial approaches; the 2024 roadmap identifies complete, transferable chamber twins as unfinished.
why: Cuts costly process-development loops and makes recipe transfer more reliable.
key_works: Oehrlein et al. (2024), [“Future of plasma etching for microelectronics: Challenges and opportunities”](https://doi.org/10.1116/6.0003579).

title: CMP control of dishing and rare surface damage
open: Predict and control local dishing, erosion, scratches, and wafer-scale nonuniformity simultaneously across mixed materials and changing pad/slurry histories.
status: CMP has decades of industrial success; a 2025 review finds benchmark, labeling, and transferability gaps, including incomplete modeling of dishing and within-wafer nonuniformity.
why: Makes dense interconnects and bonding surfaces reproducible.
key_works: Winkler et al. (2025), [“Machine learning in chemical–mechanical planarization: A comprehensive review of trends, applications, and challenges”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aei.2025.103663).

title: Traceable flow standards for reactive process gases
open: Calibrate hazardous and reactive gas delivery directly, including small transient flows, without relying on poorly known conversion factors from an inert calibration gas.
status: NIST's 2025–2026 program reports improved low-flow standards; gas-specific thermophysical data and hazardous-gas traceability remain active work.
why: Reduces recipe variation between tools and chemical suppliers.
key_works: NIST (2025–2026), [“Gas Flow and Properties: Standards and Models for Flow Metering Semiconductor Gases at Flows from 10 μL/min to 1 L/min”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/gas-flow-and-properties-standards-and-models-flow-metering-semiconductor-gases).

title: Nondestructive buried-device nanotomography at fab throughput
open: Recover nanometre-scale transistor and interconnect geometry and elemental contrast inside intact semiconductor structures rapidly enough for process control, with traceable spatial uncertainty.
status: X-ray tomography is established; NIST's project launched in 2023 targets the missing nanoscale, element-specific capabilities and practical measurement gaps.
why: Inspects hidden defects without consuming every measured device.
key_works: NIST (2024–2026), [“Nanoscale, Element-Specific X-ray Imaging for Integrated Circuit Metrology”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/nanoscale-element-specific-x-ray-imaging-integrated-circuit-metrology).

title: Quantitative three-dimensional analytical electron tomography
open: Reconstruct complex device composition and geometry at atomic or near-atomic resolution while controlling missing-angle artifacts, beam damage, and reconstruction uncertainty.
status: Atomic imaging is real; NIST's ongoing project distinguishes quantitative three-dimensional analysis from conventional projection images and aims to automate it.
why: Locates interface defects and material intermixing that two-dimensional sections miss.
key_works: NIST (2024–2026), [“Advanced Analytical Electron Tomography for Materials Development and Failure Analysis in Semiconductor Devices”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/advanced-analytical-electron-tomography-materials-development-and-failure-analysis).

title: Unbiased atom-probe reconstruction of heterogeneous devices
open: Quantify composition and dopant positions across interfaces with different evaporation fields, correcting trajectory and detection biases using transferable reference specimens.
status: Atom-probe tomography already provides subnanometer chemical maps; NIST is developing semiconductor-specific methods and reference materials to improve quantitative accuracy.
why: Separates true segregation and dopant clustering from reconstruction artifacts.
key_works: NIST (2024–2025), [“Atom Probe Tomography: Nanostructured Semiconductor Materials, Interfaces, and Devices”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/atom-probe-tomography-nanostructured-semiconductor-materials-interfaces-and).

title: Identifiable optical metrology for complex 3D shapes
open: Determine which combinations of angles, wavelengths, and polarization uniquely constrain buried geometry, rather than returning different plausible shapes with similar scattering spectra.
status: Scatterometry is industrially established; newer DUV/EUV computational microscopy reaches high dimensional sensitivity, but sensitivity alone does not guarantee identifiable geometry.
why: Prevents precise-looking but structurally incorrect process measurements.
key_works: NIST (living project), [“DUV/EUV Nanoscopy for Imaging Nanostructures”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/duveuv-nanoscopy-imaging-nanostructures); NIST (2024–2026), [“EUV Scatterometry”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/euv-scatterometry).

title: Matrix-matched ultratrace impurity standards
open: Produce certified reference materials for relevant semiconductor matrices and near-surface contaminants so that purity assays remain comparable when suppliers or materials change.
status: NIST's 2025–2026 program explicitly identifies missing matrix-matched standards and surface hydrogen/boron reference needs; existing calibrants can introduce matrix-dependent uncertainty.
why: Makes material qualification and contamination attribution defensible.
key_works: NIST (2025–2026), [“Metrology of Purity and Contaminants in Solid Materials”](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/metrology-purity-and-contaminants-solid-materials).

title: Unknown contaminants in ultrapure cleaning liquids
open: Identify unknown organic contaminants at yield-relevant concentrations, distinguish them from sampling contamination, and establish which species actually damage devices.
status: The problem persists despite mature ultrapure-water systems; NIST's September 2026 research call explicitly seeks targeted and untargeted methods at lower detection limits.
why: Detects yield losses that bulk purity specifications cannot explain.
key_works: NIST (2026), [“Analytical Chemistry Research Associate for Advancing Chemical Metrology for Semiconductor Cleaning Chemicals”](https://www.nist.gov/careers/associate-positions/1921281).

title: Causal attribution of rare fab yield excursions
open: Identify the process step and contaminant responsible for a yield excursion when defects appear much later and wafers share tools, materials, and maintenance histories.
status: Yield engineering is mature; the 2024 IRDS yield roadmap still connects contamination requirements to increasingly difficult defect conditions and measurement limits.
why: Shortens costly investigations and avoids ineffective process changes.
key_works: IEEE IRDS team (2024), [“Yield Enhancement”](https://irds.ieee.org/images/files/pdf/2024/2024IRDS_YE.pdf).

title: Traceable edge-placement error in three dimensions
open: Combine measurements from different tools into a defensible uncertainty budget for relative feature positions, including buried structures and front-to-back alignment.
status: Overlay and critical-dimension metrology have long histories; the 2024 IRDS metrology chapter, published in 2025, identifies new measurement and standardization needs for complex structures.
why: Prevents shorts and opens caused by individually acceptable but misregistered features.
key_works: Obeng et al. (2025), [“International Roadmap for Devices and Systems 2024: Metrology”](https://www.nist.gov/publications/international-roadmap-devices-and-systems-tm-2024-metrology).

title: Compositional proof of speculative multicore silicon
open: Scale machine-checked refinement proofs to industrial speculative multicore RTL, including weak-memory behavior, coherence, exceptions, and implementation transformations without rebuilding the proof for every configuration.
status: Hardware proofs are decades old; Kami demonstrated parameterized coherent RISC-V systems in 2017. Automation and coverage of substantially more complex implementations remain the scaling target.
why: Reduces processor bugs that escape simulation and appear after fabrication.
key_works: Choi et al. (2017), [“Kami: A Platform for High-Level Parametric Hardware Specification and its Modular Verification”](https://doi.org/10.1145/3110268).

title: Sound analog–digital co-verification
open: Prove mixed-signal properties using analog abstractions whose approximation errors remain bounded through feedback, mode changes, and digital control, at practical whole-system scale.
status: Formal analog methods and mixed-signal integration examples exist; recent work still relies on restricted representations rather than universal transistor-to-system certificates.
why: Verifies failures that cross the boundary between digital logic and continuous dynamics.
key_works: Mohanty and Gadde (2024), [“Analogous Alignments: Digital ‘Formally’ meets Analog”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15013); SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, “Design, Modeling, Test, and Standards”](https://srcmapt.org/chapter9/).

title: Analog layout generation that preserves measured performance
open: Generate layouts from specifications across new circuit families and process kits while reliably preserving matching, noise, parasitics, and yield with little manual intervention.
status: ALIGN established an open modular flow in 2019; coverage of arbitrary analog topology and silicon-validated portability remains incomplete.
why: Removes a major manual bottleneck in sensor, RF, and mixed-signal design.
key_works: Kunal et al. (2019), [“ALIGN: Open-Source Analog Layout Automation from the Ground Up”](https://doi.org/10.1145/3316781.3323471).

title: Placement optimized for actual routed outcomes
open: Efficiently optimize placement against final routed timing, congestion, and manufacturability rather than proxies that can improve while the finished design worsens.
status: GPU placement acceleration is established; DREAMPlace reported large speedups in 2019. Closing the gap between placement objectives and downstream physical outcomes remains a distinct problem.
why: Reduces routing failures and repeated physical-design iterations.
key_works: Lin et al. (2019), [“DREAMPlace: Deep Learning Toolkit-Enabled GPU Acceleration for Modern VLSI Placement”](https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2019-06_dreamplace-deep-learning-toolkit-enabled-gpu-acceleration-modern-vlsi-placement).

title: Calibrated extreme-tail timing and yield prediction
open: Estimate very small failure probabilities with defensible confidence under correlated, non-Gaussian process variation and operating-history shifts, using far fewer simulations than brute-force sampling.
status: Statistical timing analysis is established, and commercial high-sigma tools are powerful. Their existence does not settle calibrated uncertainty when the assumed variation model itself is wrong.
why: Avoids both hidden fleet-scale failures and excessive design guardbands.
key_works: Blaauw et al. (2008), [“Statistical Timing Analysis: From Basic Principles to State of the Art”](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCAD.2007.907047); Cadence (2026), [“Accelerated High Sigma Exploration and Circuit Yield Verification with Spectre FMC Analysis”](https://www.cadence.com/en_US/home/resources/videos/tools/custom-ic-analog-rf-design/accelerated-high-sigma-exploration-and-circuit-yield.html).

title: Glitch-power prediction across workloads and technologies
open: Predict energy from narrow pulses and hazards at large-design speed, including correlated input timing and realistic workloads, without a transistor-level simulation of every transition.
status: A 2024 study improved cell-specific pulse filtering in 32 nm simulations; accurate transfer across libraries, operating points, and large heterogeneous designs remains the target.
why: Makes power budgets and optimization reflect physical switching activity.
key_works: Villegas and Vourkas (2024), [“A Gate-Level Power Estimation Approach with a Comprehensive Definition of Thresholds for Classification and Filtering of Inertial Glitch Pulses”](https://doi.org/10.3390/jlpea14030041).

title: Composable electrical–thermal–mechanical chiplet design
open: Combine chiplet and package models across suppliers so that coupled electrical, thermal, mechanical, and optical constraints can be optimized consistently before fabrication.
status: Individual solvers and chiplet products exist; MAPT 2.0 identifies missing data semantics, interfaces, and integrated optimization capabilities.
why: Prevents local component optimization from producing an unworkable assembled system.
key_works: SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, “Design, Modeling, Test, and Standards”](https://srcmapt.org/chapter9/).

title: Error-bounded full-system parasitic extraction
open: Extract broadband electrical parasitics for huge heterogeneous three-dimensional systems with controlled error, including realistic materials and cross-scale coupling, within design-iteration budgets.
status: FastCap established accelerated extraction in 1991; today's multi-material, broadband package-scale problem goes beyond its original electrostatic formulation.
why: Predicts signal integrity and coupling without prohibitive full-wave computation.
key_works: Nabors and White (1991), [“FastCap: A Multipole Accelerated 3-D Capacitance Extraction Program”](https://ieee-ceda.org/media/fastcap-multipole-accelerated-3-d-capacitance-extraction-program); SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, Chapter 9](https://srcmapt.org/chapter9/).

title: Workload-dependent lifetime prediction and optimization
open: Predict joint circuit degradation from traps, hot carriers, temperature, and interconnect stress under changing workloads, then optimize without assuming independent constant-rate aging mechanisms.
status: Individual reliability models and recovery effects are well studied; translating stochastic device history into trustworthy whole-product lifetime remains incomplete.
why: Extends useful life while reducing unnecessarily conservative voltage and timing margins.
key_works: Grasser, ed. (2013/2014), [“Bias Temperature Instability for Devices and Circuits”](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4614-7909-3).

title: Transferable and reproducible learned chip placement
open: Establish when learned placers outperform strong conventional baselines on genuinely unseen designs and technologies, including training cost, post-route metrics, and repeated runs.
status: Mirhoseini et al. reported successful deployment in 2021; independent open assessments and the 2024 addendum show why evaluation protocol and transfer claims need explicit evidence.
why: Distinguishes reusable design intelligence from benchmark-specific optimization.
key_works: Mirhoseini et al. (2021), [“A graph placement methodology for fast chip design”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03544-w); Cheng et al. (2023), [“Assessment of Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11014).

title: Public advanced-node PDKs calibrated to measured silicon
open: Provide openly usable advanced-node process kits with validated devices, variation, extraction, reliability, and manufacturing rules, together with enough measured data to test their accuracy.
status: ASAP7 provides a predictive research kit, explicitly not tied to a foundry; open mature-node kits improve access but do not replace measured advanced-node enablement.
why: Makes cutting-edge design research reproducible outside privileged foundry relationships.
key_works: Clark et al. (2016), [“ASAP7: A 7-nm finFET predictive process design kit”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mejo.2016.04.006).

title: Public RTL-to-measured-silicon benchmark chains
open: Release linked specifications, RTL, tool versions, layouts, fabrication metadata, and measured power/performance/yield across multiple designs and processes, with licenses permitting independent reruns.
status: OpenROAD and open PDKs supply substantial pieces; complete, longitudinal, multi-foundry measurement chains remain a proposed community infrastructure target.
why: Tests whether EDA improvements survive fabrication and real workloads.
key_works: Ajayi et al. (2019), [“OpenROAD: Toward a Self-Driving, Open-Source Digital Layout Implementation Tool Chain”](https://www.ece.umn.edu/users/sachin/conf/gomactech19.pdf); SkyWater/Google (living documentation), [“Current Status—Experimental Preview”](https://skywater-pdk.readthedocs.io/en/main/status.html).

title: Tenfold improvement of a declared ADC energy frontier
open: Proposed moonshot: reduce total conversion-system energy tenfold below a specified measured frontier at fixed input bandwidth, SNDR, and linearity, including clocks, references, and calibration.
status: ADC performance has improved for decades; Murmann's 1997–2026 survey supplies measured comparison points. A universal tenfold improvement is not asserted to be physically possible.
why: Reduces the conversion overhead that can dominate sensors and accelerators.
key_works: Murmann (2026), [“ADC Performance Survey 1997–2026”](https://github.com/bmurmann/ADC-survey).

title: Identifiable blind calibration of interleaved ADCs
open: Characterize which unknown input signals permit simultaneous blind estimation of offset, gain, bandwidth, and timing mismatch; build low-overhead calibration that remains stable as those parameters drift.
status: Many background algorithms exist; Zhi et al. demonstrated combined mismatch correction in 2024. Signal-dependent identifiability and broader channel dynamics remain separate questions.
why: Maintains high-speed conversion accuracy without dedicated calibration interruptions.
key_works: Zhi et al. (2024), [“Spectrum distribution-based blind calibration method of mismatches for time-interleaved ADCs”](https://doi.org/10.1049/ell2.70030).

title: Efficient broadband sub-THz CMOS power amplification
open: Achieve useful transmitted power, modulation linearity, bandwidth, and efficiency together near transistor frequency limits, including on-chip combining and real package losses.
status: Sub-THz CMOS amplifiers are already demonstrated; a 2025 review documents continuing trade-offs among gain, output power, efficiency, and architecture.
why: Makes dense high-data-rate radios practical without excessive heat or array size.
key_works: Lee et al. (2025), [“6G communications through sub-Terahertz CMOS power amplifiers: Design challenges and trends”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2025.e43393).

title: Event-pixel noise rejection without losing weak signals
open: Reduce false events from dark current, threshold mismatch, and illumination flicker while preserving low-contrast changes, latency, and power across pixel populations and temperature.
status: Event sensors have been deployed for years; the 2022 survey describes their advantages and continuing sensor, noise, and evaluation challenges.
why: Makes asynchronous vision dependable outside controlled demonstrations.
key_works: Gallego et al. (2022), [“Event-Based Vision: A Survey”](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAMI.2020.3008413).

title: Consumer-cost MEMS inertial navigation without frequent recalibration
open: Maintain navigation-useful bias stability and scale-factor accuracy through temperature, vibration, shock, and aging at a declared consumer-level cost and power budget.
status: High-performance MEMS gyroscopes exist; the 2025 review compares operating modes with different unresolved accuracy, robustness, and implementation trade-offs.
why: Provides reliable positioning when satellite or external references are unavailable.
key_works: Chen et al. (2025), [“MEMS gyroscopes in different operation modes: A review”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.measurement.2025.116996).

title: Predictable lifetime of microscopic vacuum packages
open: Predict and certify vacuum retention in tiny MEMS cavities from leak, permeation, outgassing, and getter measurements under realistic thermal histories without waiting the full service lifetime.
status: Wafer-level vacuum packages are established; Aydin and colleagues demonstrated multiple integrity measurements in 2024. General accelerated-life extrapolation remains a different task.
why: Stabilizes resonators, inertial sensors, and uncooled infrared detectors.
key_works: Aydin, Akar, and Akin (2024), [“Wafer Level Vacuum Packaging of MEMS-Based Uncooled Infrared Sensors”](https://doi.org/10.3390/mi15080935).

title: Masking proofs that survive physical implementation
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Connect composable leakage-security proofs to measured CMOS behavior including glitches, unequal delays, coupling, and process variation, with affordable implementation overhead.
status: Robust probing models solved important formal subproblems; 2024 analysis demonstrates why eliminating glitches alone does not settle delay-induced leakage.
why: Gives cryptographic hardware guarantees that better match fabricated circuits.
key_works: Faust et al. (2017/2018), [“Composable Masking Schemes in the Presence of Physical Defaults and the Robust Probing Model”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/711); Müller, Lammers, and Moradi (2024), [“A Deep Analysis of two Glitch-Free Hardware Masking Schemes SESYM and LMDPL”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/035).

title: Security composition across untrusted chiplets
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Enforce and verify isolation when a purchased die or interposer may be malicious, including shared power, clocks, thermal paths, debug features, and communication links.
status: Conventional chip security and chiplet interfaces supply partial protections; MAPT 2.0 identifies end-to-end heterogeneous-system trust as an unresolved architectural problem.
why: Enables a supplier ecosystem without requiring every component to share one trust boundary.
key_works: SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, “Security & Privacy”](https://srcmapt.org/chapter3/).

title: PUF entropy and reliability over device lifetime
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Certify usable secret entropy after public helper data, environmental drift, aging, and learned modeling attacks, while meeting explicit key-reconstruction failure targets.
status: PUF constructions and fuzzy extraction have decades of study; Maes's 2013 treatment formalizes the properties, but no single device metric proves all lifecycle guarantees.
why: Makes low-cost silicon identity and key storage dependable.
key_works: Maes (2013), [“Physically Unclonable Functions: Constructions, Properties and Applications”](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-41395-7).

title: Representative multi-fab fault-detection benchmarks
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Share time-resolved tool, recipe, maintenance, and yield data with meaningful fault labels and held-out fabs, so algorithms can be evaluated on real distribution shifts and rare failures.
status: SECOM has been public since 2008 but contains only 1,567 production examples; it does not provide the proposed cross-fab longitudinal coverage.
why: Makes claimed predictive-maintenance and yield improvements externally testable.
key_works: McCann and Johnston (2008), [“SECOM”](https://doi.org/10.24432/C54305).

title: Linked layout–process–failure datasets
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Build access-controlled or public datasets connecting exact layout neighborhoods and full process histories to spatial defect maps and electrical failures, with preserved provenance and leakage-resistant splits.
status: Fabs collect many relevant signals; MAPT 2.0 describes fragmented data and missing lineage/interoperability. Joining and sharing these layers remains a proposed dataset target.
why: Supports causal yield models rather than image-only defect classifiers.
key_works: SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, “Digital Twins”](https://srcmapt.org/chapter12/).

title: Rowhammer protection with verified controller–DRAM contracts
subfield: Hardware security and shared experimental data
open: Guarantee disturbance protection for specified worst-case access patterns and device populations while bounding memory, refresh, energy, and performance overhead; verify that controllers actually enforce the required contract.
status: Known since 2014; McSee's 2025 measurements expose gaps between DRAM mitigation requirements and controller behavior. Existing mitigations do not settle universal low-overhead protection.
why: Prevents physical memory interference from breaking software isolation.
key_works: Jattke et al. (2025), [“McSee: Evaluating Advanced Rowhammer Attacks and Defenses via Automated DRAM Traffic Analysis”](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/jattke).

title: Room-temperature continuous-wave electrically injected group-IV laser
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Demonstrate a room-temperature, continuously electrically driven GeSn/SiGeSn laser coupled into a useful on-chip waveguide, with efficient, sustained operation.
status: Pursued since the 1990s; Seidel and colleagues demonstrated electrical continuous-wave lasing in 2024, limited to 35 K. Optical pumping and pulsed electrical operation establish partial feasibility.
why: Completes a group-IV optical source platform without separately assembled III–V gain chips.
key_works: Seidel et al. (2024), [*Continuous-wave electrically pumped multi-quantum-well laser based on group-IV semiconductors*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54873-z).
aliases: Electrically pumped silicon-compatible laser; group-IV laser temperature problem.

title: Isolator-free quantum-dot lasers under realistic reflections
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Establish operating envelopes and lifetime-qualified laser designs that remain coherent across changing package reflections, temperature, drive current, and wavelength, without a discrete isolator.
status: Feedback instability has been studied for decades. Dong and colleagues demonstrated turnkey external-cavity locking of silicon-grown quantum-dot lasers in 2024; immunity across deployed links remains a stronger requirement.
why: Removes bulky isolation components and improves optical-package cost and density.
key_works: Dong et al. (2024), [*Turnkey locking of quantum-dot lasers directly grown on Si*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-024-01413-2).

title: Comb-driven optical links with autonomous wavelength management
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Operate many wavelength channels from one integrated comb source while maintaining channel power, wavelength alignment, modulation fidelity, and automatic recovery across package-temperature changes.
status: A 2010s–2020s scaling problem. Ling and colleagues demonstrated electrically driven, turnkey microcomb generation in 2024; a source demonstration does not establish the yield and uptime of the complete wavelength-multiplexed link.
why: Replaces numerous independently stabilized lasers in dense optical interconnects.
key_works: Ling et al. (2024), [*Electrically empowered microcomb laser*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-48544-2).

title: Sub-picojoule optical I/O including all overheads
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Deliver an optical I/O system below one picojoule per delivered bit counting lasers, drivers, receivers, tuning, coding, and idle overhead under realistic traffic and temperatures.
status: Active for over a decade. Wan and colleagues' 2025 review describes component and co-design progress, but identifies sub-picojoule total-link energy and petabit integration as continuing system objectives.
why: Reduces the communication energy constraining distributed computing.
key_works: Wan et al. (2025, online), [*Integrating silicon photonics with complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technologies*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44287-025-00223-0).

title: Self-maintaining large programmable photonic meshes
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Keep large interferometer meshes accurately configured during continuous operation despite thermal crosstalk, actuator drift, imperfect couplers, and nonuniform loss, with control overhead that grows acceptably with circuit size.
status: A central 2010s–2020s challenge. Self-configuration and characterization have been demonstrated, including Pérez-López and colleagues' 2020 experiments, while scalable continuous correction remains application-dependent.
why: Makes general-purpose photonic processors and switches practical beyond laboratory calibration.
key_works: Pérez-López et al. (2020), [*Multipurpose self-configuration of programmable photonic circuits*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19608-w); Bogaerts et al. (2020), [*Programmable photonic circuits*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2764-0).

title: Photonic circuit density without prohibitive crosstalk
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Increase usable photonic component density substantially while jointly controlling optical leakage, RF coupling, thermal interactions, routing loss, and calibration power in a manufactured circuit.
status: The 2024 silicon-photonics roadmap identifies spacing between components, rather than minimum waveguide width alone, as a major density constraint; large circuits exist but do not remove these coupled limits.
why: Enables larger useful functions within optical-chip area and power budgets.
key_works: Shekhar et al. (2024), [*Roadmapping the next generation of silicon photonics*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-44750-0).

title: Foundry-integrated broadband optical isolation
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Integrate broadband, low-loss optical isolation with semiconductor photonics at high manufacturing yield, preserving isolation across temperature, polarization, optical power, and long-term package stress.
status: Decades old. Lapointe and colleagues demonstrated hybrid Faraday isolation without external magnets or lenses in 2025, exceeding 25 dB across the C-band; foundry and package qualification remains separate.
why: Protects integrated lasers and precision optical measurements from destabilizing reflections.
key_works: Lapointe et al. (2025), [*Passive broadband Faraday isolator for hybrid integration to photonic circuits without lens and external magnet*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-024-01601-0).

title: Manufacturable Pockels photonics with stable interfaces
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Produce heterogeneous electro-optic photonics with simultaneously low optical loss, low drive voltage, high bandwidth, uniform wafer performance, and stable bonded interfaces over service life.
status: Accelerated during the 2010s. Wang and colleagues demonstrated wafer-scale lithium-tantalate photonics in 2024, extending the options beyond lithium niobate; production-scale multimaterial yield and qualification remain combined challenges.
why: Adds efficient modulation to silicon-based communication and sensing chips.
key_works: Wang et al. (2024), [*Lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuits for volume manufacturing*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07369-1).

title: Efficient colour-stable sub-2-micrometre red microLEDs
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Achieve high red-emission efficiency and stable colour at display-relevant low currents in sub-2-µm pixels, while maintaining array uniformity and operating lifetime.
status: A persistent microdisplay bottleneck since the 2010s. Kong and colleagues reported 6.5% external quantum efficiency from 1.5-µm InGaN red devices in 2025; spectral shifts and complete display performance remain relevant limitations.
why: Enables bright, energy-efficient full-colour near-eye displays.
key_works: Kong et al. (2025), [*1-nm-thick epitaxial AlN passivation for highly efficient flexible InGaN red micro-LEDs*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60886-z).

title: Closing the yellow-green LED efficiency gap
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Produce direct-emission 535–570 nm semiconductor LEDs with high wall-plug efficiency across useful current densities, without unacceptable colour shift, droop, or lifetime penalties.
status: Known for decades as the green gap. Hybrid quantum-well structures improved yellow-green emission in Jiang and colleagues' 2015 experiments; material quality, carrier localization, and polarization remain coupled design issues.
why: Improves colour mixing and reduces lighting and display conversion losses.
key_works: Jiang et al. (2015), [*Realization of high-luminous-efficiency InGaN light-emitting diodes in the “green gap” range*](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep10883).

title: Economical defect-free megapixel microLED assembly
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Assemble, electrically connect, inspect, and repair millions of RGB emitters with production throughput and a final defective-pixel rate compatible with premium displays, including ageing-induced failures.
status: A 2010s–2020s manufacturing challenge. Chang and colleagues demonstrated 99.99% simultaneous RGB transfer yield in 2023; that yield still leaves substantial repair demand when multiplied across millions of emitters.
why: Converts promising microLED devices into affordable large displays.
key_works: Chang et al. (2023), [*Concurrent self-assembly of RGB microLEDs for next-generation displays*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-05889-w).

title: Qualified cadmium-free blue quantum-dot displays
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Preserve high blue efficiency, colour purity, and low degradation through high-resolution patterning, encapsulation, and realistic high-brightness display operation using cadmium-free quantum dots.
status: A long-standing QLED bottleneck. Wu and colleagues reported 24.7% peak external quantum efficiency from ZnSeTeS-based pure-blue devices in 2025; material-level gains still require reproducible patterned-display qualification.
why: Supports efficient full-colour displays with less dependence on cadmium-containing emitters.
key_works: Wu et al. (2025), [*Homogeneous ZnSeTeS quantum dots for efficient and stable pure-blue LEDs*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08645-4).

title: Fully integrated long-range parallel coherent lidar
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Combine laser, amplification, beam steering, coherent reception, and control into a compact system that jointly meets long-range, wide-field, frame-rate, eye-safety, and environmental-robustness requirements.
status: Intensively pursued since the 2010s. Chen and colleagues demonstrated microcomb-driven parallel silicon-photonic FMCW imaging in 2025, including metre-scale ranging; integrated power budgets and field performance remain harder combined targets.
why: Enables compact, high-resolution depth sensing for autonomous systems.
key_works: Chen et al. (2025), [*Single soliton microcomb combined with optical phased array for parallel FMCW LiDAR*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56483-9).

title: Efficient waveguide microwave–optical transduction
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Increase conversion efficiency in broadband travelling-wave electro-optomechanical interfaces while preserving low added noise, high dynamic range, and cascaded optical-signal integrity.
status: An active 2010s–2020s problem. Zhou and colleagues demonstrated envelope-preserving Brillouin transduction and channelization in 2024, but reported extrinsic quantum conversion efficiency around −54 dB under their stated accounting.
why: Connects optical processing with microwave sensing and communication without repeatedly destroying the optical signal.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2024), [*Electrically interfaced Brillouin-active waveguide for microwave photonic measurements*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-51010-8).

title: Navigation-grade integrated optical gyroscopes in the field
subfield: Integrated photonics, semiconductor light sources, and displays
open: Maintain sufficiently low bias drift and angle noise for demanding navigation in a completely integrated gyroscope under temperature cycles, vibration, ageing, and laser-power fluctuations.
status: Pursued for decades. Lai and colleagues measured Earth's rotation with a silicon-chip Brillouin ring-laser gyroscope in 2020; field-qualified navigation requires more than laboratory rotation sensitivity.
why: Enables accurate inertial navigation where external positioning signals are unavailable.
key_works: Lai et al. (2020), [*Earth rotation measured by a chip-scale ring laser gyroscope*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-020-0588-y).

title: Predicting 25-year perovskite photovoltaic service life
open: Establish validated degradation models predicting 25 years of useful module operation under combined light, heat, humidity, bias, and mechanical stress.
status: Stability has blocked deployment since the technology's 2010s rise. ISOS reporting guidance improved comparability, and newer modules pass qualification tests; those results do not alone establish multi-decade field lifetime.
why: Makes lifetime guarantees and reliable energy-yield forecasts possible.
key_works: Khenkin et al. (2020), [*Consensus statement for stability assessment and reporting for perovskite photovoltaics based on ISOS procedures*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-019-0529-5).

title: Lifetime lead containment after photovoltaic module damage
open: Demonstrate lead capture that remains effective after decades of weathering and realistic combinations of cracking, fire, flooding, and recycling, without sacrificing performance or economical manufacture.
status: A concern since the 2010s. Chen and colleagues substantially reduced lead release from damaged mini-modules with ion-exchange resins in 2020; lifetime and failure-scenario validation remains broader.
why: Enables safer deployment and end-of-life handling of lead-containing absorbers.
key_works: Chen et al. (2020), [*Trapping lead in perovskite solar modules with abundant and low-cost cation-exchange resins*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-020-00716-2).

title: Closing the perovskite cell-to-module production gap
open: Reproduce small-cell performance across metre-scale production modules while controlling coating nonuniformity, shunts, interconnection losses, production yield, and durability over repeated manufacturing lots.
status: A decade-old scaling problem. Xu and colleagues reported certified 22.0% total-area efficiency on 0.72 m² modules in 2026, demonstrating major progress; consistently approaching laboratory-cell performance remains a stricter target.
why: Converts absorber efficiency gains into low-cost electricity from commercial-area modules.
key_works: Xu et al. (2026), [*Lead carboxylates passivation for metre-scale perovskite solar modules*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10994-7).

title: Stable wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskites
open: Prevent illumination- and bias-driven halide redistribution in wide-bandgap absorbers while retaining high voltage, efficient charge extraction, and scalable ambient fabrication over long operating periods.
status: Recognized since the mid-2010s. Yang and colleagues suppressed oxidation and demixing with reductive cations in 2025, reporting 23.3% cells and 700-hour mini-module testing; long-duration combined-stress performance remains open.
why: Removes a central voltage and durability constraint in tandem top cells.
key_works: Yang et al. (2025), [*Reductive cation for scalable wide-bandgap perovskite solar cells in ambient air*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41893-025-01529-5).

title: Durable narrow-bandgap tin–lead perovskite junctions
open: Stabilize complete tin–lead photovoltaic junctions against self-doping, ionic redistribution, interfacial reactions, and oxidation under simultaneous heat and illumination, without losing narrow-bandgap efficiency.
status: A persistent 2010s–2020s problem. Rombach and colleagues showed in 2025 that dominant degradation pathways change with the hole-transport material; structurally stable absorbers can still produce deteriorating devices.
why: Enables durable all-perovskite multijunction photovoltaics.
key_works: Rombach et al. (2025), [*Disentangling degradation pathways of narrow bandgap lead-tin perovskite material and photovoltaic devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58489-9).

title: Efficient durable commercial-area perovskite–silicon tandems
open: Realize greater-than-35% tandem module efficiency at commercial area together with reproducible textured-silicon integration and validated long service life.
status: Monolithic tandems emerged in the mid-2010s. Yang and colleagues' 2025 review describes cell efficiencies approaching 35%, alongside continuing scalability, voltage-loss, and stability barriers; a cell result does not establish this module-level combination.
why: Increases electricity output per installation area and reduces associated infrastructure per watt.
key_works: Yang et al. (2025), [*Towards efficient, scalable and stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-025-01732-y).

title: Lifetime-qualified reverse-bias protection for perovskite modules
open: Protect full-size perovskite modules against repeated shading and reverse-bias transients throughout service, including protection-element and interface ageing.
status: A recognized 2010s–2020s failure mode. Mohammadi and colleagues demonstrated integrated self-switching protection in a nine-cell laboratory string in 2026; long-lived commercial-module deployment remains a distinct engineering target.
why: Prevents shading-induced damage and localized heating during normal field operation.
key_works: Mohammadi et al. (2026), [*Integrated memristor for mitigating reverse-bias in perovskite solar cells*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10275-3).

title: Industrial silicon photovoltaics near the intrinsic efficiency ceiling
open: Approach 29%-class single-junction efficiency on industrial-size silicon cells while preserving manufacturing throughput, low recombination, inexpensive contacts, and module compatibility.
status: A decades-long engineering problem. Tong and colleagues reported certified 27.03% total-area efficiency over 350 cm² in 2025; remaining losses involve optical absorption, contacts, and carrier recombination.
why: Extracts more energy from the established silicon manufacturing base.
key_works: Tong et al. (2025), [*Total-area world-record efficiency of 27.03% for 350.0 cm² commercial-sized single-junction silicon solar cells*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61128-y).

title: Durable silver-free silicon solar-cell metallization
open: Replace silver with inexpensive conductors while matching contact resistance, adhesion, diffusion blocking, production yield, and multi-decade module reliability across high-efficiency silicon architectures.
status: Investigated for decades and increasingly urgent at large deployment scales. Pingel and colleagues studied copper-based screen-printed heterojunction cells in 2025; a robust process–lifetime combination remains technology-specific.
why: Reduces material cost and resource pressure from photovoltaic expansion.
key_works: Pingel et al. (2025), [*Transition from silver-to copper-based screen printed SHJ solar cells*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.solmat.2025.113593).

title: Controlling compensating defects in CdSeTe photovoltaics
open: Predictably control doping, trap populations, and band tails throughout industrial CdSeTe absorbers so that higher carrier density produces sustained voltage and fill-factor gains without lifetime penalties.
status: Defect compensation has constrained CdTe for decades. Kuciauskas and colleagues showed in 2025 that phosphorus reduced trapping and band tails, improving efficiency through a composition-sensitive route.
why: Moves thin-film photovoltaics closer to attainable conversion efficiency.
key_works: Kuciauskas et al. (2025), [*Doping with phosphorus reduces anion vacancy disorder in CdSeTe semiconductors enabling higher solar cell efficiency*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63589-7).

title: Low-voltage-loss narrow-bandgap CIGSe bottom cells
open: Minimize front- and back-interface recombination in approximately 1 eV CIGSe while retaining strong infrared absorption and compatible tandem integration at manufacturing scale.
status: Narrow-bandgap tandem optimization remains active. Zhang and colleagues demonstrated 20.26% certified narrow-bandgap cells in 2024 using gallium grading; the reported voltage deficit remained substantial.
why: Provides an efficient thin-film bottom junction for lightweight tandem photovoltaics.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2024), [*Highly efficient narrow bandgap Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells with enhanced open circuit voltage for tandem application*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54818-6).

title: Eliminating the kesterite voltage deficit
open: Suppress the bulk and interface losses behind kesterite's voltage deficit without introducing compensating defects or sacrificing manufacturable phase purity.
status: Open since the 2000s. Magnesium-assisted ordering produced 14.9%-efficient certified cells in 2025; defect activity and ordering kinetics remain intertwined.
why: Enables high-performance thin-film photovoltaics based on relatively abundant constituent elements.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025 online; 2026 issue), [*Vacancy-enhanced cation ordering via magnesium doping to enable kesterite solar cells with 14.9% certified efficiency*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01902-w).

title: Long-lived high-efficiency organic photovoltaic modules
open: Stabilize the active-layer morphology, buried interfaces, and encapsulation of high-efficiency organic modules simultaneously under illumination, damp heat, thermal cycling, and mechanical strain.
status: A decades-old deployment barrier. Qin and colleagues demonstrated approximately 18%-efficient cells retaining 94% efficiency after their damp-heat and thermal-cycling tests in 2025; long-term module-level field performance remains broader.
why: Enables lightweight, flexible, and semitransparent power generation.
key_works: Qin et al. (2025), [*Improved damp heat and thermal cycling stability of organic solar cells*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01885-8).

title: Reusable III–V growth substrates with negligible performance loss
open: Reuse III–V growth substrates through repeated rapid lift-off and regrowth without appreciable consumption, defects, yield loss, or efficiency degradation.
status: Pursued for decades. Direct GaAs reuse appeared in 2013; Neumann's 2025 sonic lift-off preserved performance, while economical repeated-cycle production remains open.
why: Could reduce III–V photovoltaic cost for terrestrial applications.
key_works: Neumann et al. (2025), [*Solar Cell Performance after Exfoliation Using Sonic Liftoff*](https://doi.org/10.1002/solr.202500049); Cheng et al. (2013), [*Epitaxial lift-off process for gallium arsenide substrate reuse and flexible electronics*](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms2583).

title: Net-power-gaining singlet-fission silicon photovoltaics
open: Integrate a singlet-fission sensitizer with silicon so that extra collected charge exceeds added optical and electrical losses under standard sunlight, with stable operation and scalable manufacture.
status: Investigated for decades. Baldo and colleagues' 2025 perspective outlines progress and integration requirements; efficient exciton generation or transfer alone does not establish a net photovoltaic power benefit.
why: Harvests high-energy photons more efficiently without a conventional additional junction.
key_works: Baldo et al. (2025), [*Singlet Fission Provides a Scalable Pathway to High Efficiency Silicon Photovoltaics*](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsenergylett.5c01944).

title: Increasing-distance quantum error correction in silicon
open: Demonstrate repeated silicon error correction with logical error rates decreasing as code distance increases, including leakage, measurement errors, and parallel operation.
status: Pursued since spin-qubit proposals. In 2026, donor clusters implemented a [[4,2,2]] detection code and shuttled spins performed weight-four parity checks; scalable error suppression remains unestablished.
why: Converts high-quality physical spins into dependable computational resources.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [*Universal logical operations in a silicon quantum processor*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-026-02140-1); Undseth et al. (2026), [*Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10766-3).

title: Foundry-wide high-fidelity spin-qubit yield
open: Manufacture large arrays in which the joint distribution of initialization, readout, single-qubit, and two-qubit performance supports fault tolerance without selecting a few exceptional devices.
status: A central 2010s–2020s scaling question. Steinacker and colleagues reported greater-than-99% one- and two-qubit control in four foundry-made two-qubit devices in 2025; wafer-scale array yield remains a stronger statistical requirement.
why: Makes semiconductor manufacturing scale translate into usable quantum processors.
key_works: Steinacker et al. (2025), [*Industry-compatible silicon spin-qubit unit cells exceeding 99% fidelity*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09531-9).

title: Uniform useful valley splitting along silicon qubit networks
open: Engineer predictable, sufficiently large valley splitting throughout silicon qubit and shuttling regions while maintaining low charge noise and controllable confinement.
status: Known for decades. Volmer and colleagues mapped values spanning 1.5–200 µeV in a shuttle region in 2026 and showed trajectory-based mitigation; microscopic disorder still complicates uniform operation.
why: Reduces leakage, initialization failures, and decoherence in spin architectures.
key_works: Volmer et al. (2026), [*Impact of the local valley splitting on the coherence of conveyor-belt spin shuttling in 28Si/SiGe*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74382-5).

title: Error-budget-compatible spin shuttling through networks
open: Transport spins through branching networks with bounded error and crosstalk during simultaneous loading, junction crossing, storage, and interactions.
status: Pursued since the 2010s. De Smet achieved 99.5% average spin-preservation fidelity over an effective 10 µm in 2025; Matsumoto added mobile two-qubit operations in 2026.
why: Gives semiconductor qubits flexible connectivity without one control channel per interaction.
key_works: De Smet et al. (2025), [*High-fidelity single-spin shuttling in silicon*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-025-01920-5); Matsumoto et al. (2026), [*Two-qubit logic and teleportation with mobile spin qubits in silicon*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10423-9).

title: High-fidelity microwave-photon-mediated spin gates
open: Implement deterministic entangling gates between distant gate-defined spins through a resonator with error rates suitable for repeated error correction, including photon loss, charge noise, and leakage.
status: Strong spin–photon coupling has been demonstrated since the late 2010s. Yu and colleagues demonstrated a foundry-compatible hole-spin interface in 2023; efficient coupling alone does not establish a low-error remote gate.
why: Connects separated spin registers and relaxes nearest-neighbour layout constraints.
key_works: Yu et al. (2023), [*Strong coupling between a photon and a hole spin in silicon*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-023-01332-3).

title: Fault-tolerant spin arrays above one kelvin
open: Operate a complete spin-qubit array above 1 K with initialization, measurement, gates, and idle errors collectively meeting an experimentally validated error-correction budget.
status: High-temperature operation advanced markedly in the 2020s. Huang and colleagues demonstrated algorithmic initialization and high-fidelity gates above 1 K in 2024; scaling those results under continuous control-system heat load remains open.
why: Expands available refrigeration power and simplifies dense quantum-control integration.
key_works: Huang et al. (2024), [*High-fidelity spin qubit operation and algorithmic initialization above 1 K*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07160-2).

title: Scalable cryogenic control without qubit degradation
open: Integrate control and readout for large spin arrays within cryogenic power, wiring, and area budgets while preserving fidelity during simultaneous switching and measurement.
status: A long-standing scaling barrier. Bartee and colleagues demonstrated silicon spin control with a millikelvin CMOS chip in 2025 with little gate-performance degradation; complete large-array operation adds multiplexing and thermal constraints.
why: Removes the wiring and control-hardware bottleneck to semiconductor quantum computing.
key_works: Bartee et al. (2025), [*Spin-qubit control with a milli-kelvin CMOS chip*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09157-x).

title: Autonomous calibration that scales beyond individual spin qubits
open: Automatically initialize and maintain large interacting spin arrays despite device variation, hysteresis, drift, and failed elements, with measured convergence and bounded interruption of computation.
status: Automated tuning developed through the 2010s. Schuff and colleagues demonstrated autonomous progression from an unpowered device to single-qubit control in 2026; reliable multiqubit maintenance is a larger control problem.
why: Prevents manual calibration effort from growing with every added qubit.
key_works: Schuff et al. (2026), [*Fully autonomous tuning of a spin qubit*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-025-01562-4).

title: Correlated-error control under parallel spin operations
open: Characterize and suppress correlated gate and readout errors during simultaneous operations, distinguishing local errors from crosstalk and shared environmental noise.
status: A recognized scaling concern. Mądzik and colleagues demonstrated parallel operation of two exchange-only qubits in 2025 without degrading control quality; many-array, many-operation error correlations remain insufficiently constrained.
why: Validates the locality assumptions on which useful error-correction thresholds depend.
key_works: Mądzik et al. (2025), [*Operating two exchange-only qubits in parallel*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09767-5).

title: Deterministic indistinguishable emitter arrays with efficient coupling
open: Fabricate large arrays of addressable, spectrally matched quantum dots efficiently coupled into photonic circuits while maintaining single-photon purity and mutual indistinguishability.
status: Pursued since the 2000s. O'Hara and colleagues edge-coupled ten site-controlled dots to silicon-nitride waveguides in 2026, with inferred coupling around 5%; simultaneous high efficiency and large-array indistinguishability remain harder goals.
why: Supplies repeatable quantum-light resources without extensive emitter selection.
key_works: O'Hara et al. (2026), [*Site-controlled quantum dot arrays edge-coupled to integrated silicon nitride waveguides and devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74664-y).

title: Near-unity useful indistinguishability of telecom quantum-dot photons
open: Combine near-unity raw photon indistinguishability, high extraction efficiency, fast deterministic excitation, and stable electrically tunable telecom emission across independent emitters.
status: A two-decade objective. Hauser and colleagues demonstrated raw two-photon interference visibility up to 91.7% from a C-band quantum-dot source in 2026; scaling high visibility and brightness across independent sources remains open.
why: Improves the success and fidelity of fibre-based quantum networking.
key_works: Hauser et al. (2026), [*Deterministic and highly indistinguishable single photons in the telecom C-band*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68336-0).

title: Fault-tolerant graph states from semiconductor quantum dots
open: Generate and connect long photonic graph states with loss and correlated spin-induced errors below a complete fault-tolerant computation threshold, at useful resource-generation rates.
status: Proposed in the 2000s. Huet and colleagues demonstrated reconfigurable graph-state generation from a cavity-coupled quantum dot in 2025; high-quality long-range entanglement and graph fusion remain essential scaling steps.
why: Provides deterministic resources for measurement-based quantum computers.
key_works: Huet et al. (2025), [*Deterministic and reconfigurable graph state generation with a single solid-state quantum emitter*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59693-3).

title: Complete silicon-carbide quantum-network nodes
open: Integrate coherent registers, efficient spin–photon interfaces, tuning, and routing into SiC nodes that repeatedly establish remote entanglement while preserving stored quantum information.
