status: Rapid progress since the 2010s. Hu and colleagues integrated an entangled electron–nuclear register into a SiC waveguide in 2024, retaining about 0.88 state fidelity; a complete network node requires additional capabilities together.
why: Links semiconductor fabrication with distributed quantum computing and sensing.
key_works: Hu et al. (2024), [*Room-temperature waveguide integrated quantum register in a semiconductor photonic platform*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54606-2).

title: Loss-inclusive fault tolerance in foundry photonic quantum processors
open: Demonstrate scalable logical protection in foundry-made photonic hardware after accounting for every source, routing, switch, coupling, and detection loss, including feed-forward latency and resource overhead.
status: A 2010s–2020s challenge. PsiQuantum demonstrated high-fidelity integrated components in 2025, with qubit fidelities conditional on detection; loss-inclusive logical operation remains a stronger requirement.
why: Establishes whether semiconductor manufacturing can supply economically useful photonic quantum computation.
key_works: PsiQuantum team (2025), [*A manufacturable platform for photonic quantum computing*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08820-7).

title: Unambiguous non-Abelian Majorana operations in semiconductor hybrids
open: Demonstrate noncommuting exchange or equivalent measurement-only operations on semiconductor–superconductor Majorana modes, while excluding ordinary Andreev-state explanations and establishing a protected operating regime.
status: Pursued since 2010-era nanowire proposals. Microsoft Azure Quantum's 2025 parity-readout experiment explicitly allowed trivial and topological interpretations; parity measurement alone is not non-Abelian braiding.
why: Tests a proposed protected quantum-computing platform's physical basis.
key_works: Microsoft Azure Quantum and Aghaee et al. (2025), [*Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2).

title: Sub-200-nanometre hybrid bonding at production yield
open: Manufacture sub-200-nm wafer-to-wafer interconnects with acceptable yield, overlay, throughput, and lifetime across wafers and production lots.
status: A 2010s–2020s scaling problem. Imec and EV Group demonstrated 200-nm-pitch routable test structures on 300-mm wafers in 2026, with pad overlay below 40 nm; production qualification and further pitch reduction remain separate requirements.
why: Increases communication density between vertically integrated semiconductor tiers.
key_works: Imec and EV Group (2026), [*Imec and EV Group demonstrate wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding with 200nm interconnect pitch and record high overlay accuracy*](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/imec-and-ev-group-demonstrate-wafer-wafer-hybrid-bonding-200nm-interconnect-pitch-and-record).

title: Submicrometre die-to-wafer assembly of heterogeneous chiplets
open: Bond individually selected, heterogeneous dies at submicrometre interconnect pitch while controlling placement errors, particles, die distortion, and contact resistance at economically useful assembly throughput.
status: Pursued since the 2010s. Imec reported 2-µm-pitch die-to-wafer hybrid bonding with sub-350-nm overlay in 2024; selecting and placing separate dies imposes constraints beyond aligned whole-wafer bonding.
why: Connects known-good chiplets from different manufacturing processes without coarse interconnect penalties.
key_works: Imec (2024), [*Imec demonstrates die-to-wafer hybrid bonding with a Cu interconnect pad pitch of 2µm*](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/imec-demonstrates-die-wafer-hybrid-bonding-cu-interconnect-pad-pitch-2mm).

title: Low-temperature hybrid bonding across sensitive heterogeneous dies
open: Establish hybrid bonding recipes that simultaneously provide low resistance, strong adhesion, fine pitch, and qualified reliability within the thermal budgets of temperature-sensitive semiconductor dies.
status: A longstanding constraint intensified by stacking. Cheemalamarri demonstrated void-free low-temperature Cu/dielectric bonding using ultrathin passivation in 2026; transfer across die materials and lifetime conditions remains open.
why: Permits stacking fabricated electronic, photonic, or quantum devices.
key_works: Cheemalamarri et al. (2026), [*Void-free Cu/dielectric hybrid bonding at low-temperature enabled by ultrathin metal passivation engineering for 3D-IC applications*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44172-026-00649-w).

title: Repair of completed dense hybrid-bonded stacks
open: Replace defective dies or restore failed connections in completed fine-pitch hybrid-bonded stacks without damaging retained dies, degrading subsequent reliability, or consuming the economic benefit of repair.
status: An obstacle since dense permanent bonding became practical. Gangadharan and colleagues reported a reworkable die-to-wafer process in 2026; repairing fully processed, deeply stacked products requires broader capability than rebonding test vehicles.
why: Recovers expensive assembled systems and enables longer service lives.
key_works: Gangadharan et al. (2026), [*Reworkable Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding Process*](https://doi.org/10.1109/ECTC51846.2026.00220).

title: Rapid nondestructive imaging of buried package defects
open: Locate electrically important buried bond, via, and redistribution-layer defects throughout complete heterogeneous packages, with resolution and throughput suitable for process control and without destructive sample preparation.
status: A decades-old inspection challenge. Aidukas and colleagues achieved 4-nm-resolution X-ray tomography using burst ptychography in 2024; nanoscale imaging of selected integrated-circuit volumes does not establish whole-package manufacturing throughput.
why: Reveals hidden assembly failures before costly deployment or destructive diagnosis.
key_works: Aidukas et al. (2024), [*High-performance 4-nm-resolution X-ray tomography using burst ptychography*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07615-6).

title: Warpage control across large packaging panels
open: Keep full-panel and die warpage within assembly tolerances throughout molding, curing, debonding, and thermal cycling, despite heterogeneous layouts and variable material history.
status: A 2010s–2020s scaling challenge. Hu compared experimentally informed molding-first and redistribution-layer-first panel models in 2026; robust control across sizes, layouts, and production variation remains unresolved.
why: Prevents placement errors, cracked connections, and yield loss in larger packages.
key_works: Hu et al. (2026), [*Finite element analysis of warpage and debonding behavior in RDL-first and molding-first fan-out panel-level packaging*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-47275-2).

title: Economical known-good-die and buried-interconnect assurance
open: Screen latent die and buried interconnect defects with quantified escape rates while limiting probe damage, test-access area, and cost.
status: Known-good-die assurance dates to 1990s multichip modules. Bhoumik's 2026 survey includes prebond testing and multilayer redistribution faults; inaccessible connections and interacting faults remain difficult.
why: Avoids discarding expensive multi-die assemblies because one hidden element fails.
key_works: Bhoumik et al. (2026), [*Testing of Chiplet-Based Packages Based on Advanced Heterogeneous Integration*](https://doi.org/10.1109/MDAT.2026.3706448).

title: Qualified low-energy links between independently supplied chiplets
open: Demonstrate interoperable chiplet links across independent vendors at target bandwidth and energy per delivered bit, while maintaining error rate and recoverability under realistic voltage, temperature, ageing, and package variation.
status: A 2020s ecosystem challenge. UCIe 3.0, released in 2025, specifies 48/64-GT/s operation and expanded management capabilities; a standard enables interoperability but does not itself qualify every implementation combination.
why: Makes reusable chiplets practical components of heterogeneous systems.
key_works: UCIe Consortium (2025), [*UCIe 3.0 Specification*](https://www.uciexpress.org/specifications).

title: Lifetime prediction for electromigration in fine package interconnects
open: Predict fine-microbump and hybrid-copper-bond failure distributions under realistic currents and temperature gradients, accounting for interfaces, grain structure, and void evolution.
status: Studied since the 1960s, with mechanisms changing at small scales. Chang identified surface-diffusion-driven Sn failure in microbumps in 2018, challenging direct extrapolation from larger interconnects.
why: Supports denser package wiring without unpredictable field failures.
key_works: Chang et al. (2018), [*A new failure mechanism of electromigration by surface diffusion of Sn on Ni and Cu metallization in microbumps*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-23809-1).

title: Predictive thermal conductance of hybrid-bond interfaces
open: Predict thermal boundary conductance from bond chemistry, roughness, voids, copper-pad fraction, and ageing, with uncertainties supporting heterogeneous-stack heat-path design.
status: A 2010s–2020s integration problem. Zhang and colleagues measured thermal conductance across bonded silicon-oxide interfaces in 2026; extending individual interface measurements to patterned, defective, ageing production bonds remains open.
why: Prevents an apparently short vertical connection from becoming a thermal bottleneck.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [*Thermal conductance across bonded SiOx–SiOx interfaces in hybrid bonding process*](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0338819).

title: Thermal interface materials that retain performance throughout service
open: Maintain low contact resistance at realistic clamping pressures after years of temperature cycling, vibration, oxidation, and mechanical creep, without pump-out, dry-out, or electrically dangerous migration.
status: A decades-old problem. Cheng demonstrated a liquid-infused nanostructured composite in 2025; combining initial heat-transfer performance with long-term stability across package surfaces remains unresolved.
why: Preserves cooling as processors, accelerators, and optical modules age.
key_works: Cheng et al. (2025), [*Liquid-infused nanostructured composite as a high-performance thermal interface material for effective cooling*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56163-8).

title: Lifetime-qualified embedded microfluidic cooling
open: Integrate microfluidic cooling with high heat removal, low pumping energy, leak-free operation, cleanliness, corrosion resistance, and lifetime maintainability.
status: Pursued since the 1980s. Wu and colleagues removed 3,000 W/cm² with jet-enhanced manifold microchannels in 2025; exceptional test-device heat flux does not establish long-lived package and coolant-system reliability.
why: Enables power densities that conventional external cooling cannot economically sustain.
key_works: Wu et al. (2025), [*Jet-enhanced manifold microchannels for cooling electronics up to a heat flux of 3,000 W cm−2*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-025-01449-4).

title: Heat extraction from inner tiers of dense 3D packages
open: Remove spatially and temporally concentrated heat from interior tiers while preserving vertical connection density, mechanical strength, manufacturability, and acceptable temperature differences between dies.
status: Recognized since early 3D integration. Sharma and Ramos-Alvarado's 2026 review identifies restricted heat paths and heterogeneous hotspots; thermal vias and interlayer cooling consume space or complicate integration.
why: Increases useful stacked compute density without thermal throttling.
key_works: Sharma and Ramos-Alvarado (2026), [*Thermal management of 3-D heterogeneously integrated microelectronics: challenges and future research directions*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44172-026-00590-y).

title: Stress-compatible cooling of heterogeneous chiplet packages
open: Cool dies with different heights, stiffnesses, and thermal expansion coefficients while maintaining uniform contact and preventing underfill fatigue, delamination, or die cracking during repeated power cycling.
status: A longstanding problem intensified by heterogeneous assemblies. Sharma and Ramos-Alvarado reviewed thermal and structural constraints in 2026; improved cooling still requires package-level mechanical compatibility.
why: Converts laboratory cooling performance into reliable multichip products.
key_works: Sharma and Ramos-Alvarado (2026), [*Thermal management of 3-D heterogeneously integrated microelectronics: challenges and future research directions*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44172-026-00590-y).

title: Open packaging-material reliability data across processes
open: Build uncertainty-annotated datasets connecting underfill, molding, adhesive, and interface properties to cure history, exposure, manufacturing variation, and package failures across laboratories.
status: A longstanding barrier. NIST published Tao's 2026 dataset on one epoxy underfill's cure evolution and thermal endurance; multi-material and multi-process coverage remains incomplete.
why: Enables reproducible lifetime modelling and prevents repeated characterization of equivalent materials.
key_works: Tao et al. (2026), [*Data for Predicting Cure Evolution and Thermal Endurance of a Highly Filled Epoxy Underfill for Advanced Packaging*](https://doi.org/10.18434/mds2-4162).

title: Sub-electron global-shutter imaging at kiloframe rates
open: Combine sub-electron read noise, kiloframe-per-second UHD global-shutter capture, pixels no larger than 5 µm, and few-watt sensor power, with low image lag across the array.
status: A decades-old speed–noise trade-off. Agarwal's 2025 sensor delivered 1,100-frame/s UHD capture with 5-µm pixels and three-electron noise; sensitivity and throughput remain coupled.
why: Resolves fast, dim events without motion distortion or excessive illumination.
key_works: Agarwal et al. (2025), [*High-Frame Rate Low-Noise Global Shutter CMOS Image Sensor for High-Speed Machine Vision*](https://doi.org/10.60928/cfm9-2fol).

title: High-temperature single-exposure dynamic range without noisy gain transitions
open: Achieve flicker-free single-exposure dynamic range above 130 dB, with transition signal-to-noise ratio above 30 dB at 125 °C in approximately 2-µm pixels.
status: Pursued since the 1990s. Innocent reported 126-dB test-chip range in 2025; their product target sacrificed range to preserve high-temperature transition quality.
why: Preserves automotive lamp and shadow detail.
key_works: Innocent et al. (2025), [*2.1µm LFM Automotive Pixel with Single Photodiode and 126 dB of Single Exposure Dynamic Range*](https://doi.org/10.60928/es6a-7h7l).

title: Low-dark-count room-temperature telecom Ge–Si SPAD arrays
open: Produce CMOS-compatible Ge–Si photon-counting arrays with high telecom detection probability and low timing jitter while reducing dark events enough for weak-signal operation without cooling.
status: Pursued since the 2000s. Na demonstrated room-temperature operation in 2024, reporting 12% detection probability at 1,310 nm and dark counts of 19 kHz/µm²; array-level noise remains consequential.
why: Enables photon-counting receivers and ranging using telecom wavelengths.
key_works: Na et al. (2024), [*Room temperature operation of germanium–silicon single-photon avalanche diode*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07076-x).

title: Eliminating external optical crosstalk in SiPM assemblies
open: Suppress avalanche-triggered neighbouring SiPM events without sacrificing photon collection, timing, or usable overvoltage in complete optical assemblies.
status: Recognized since SiPM arrays spread. Lee reduced external crosstalk using filters in 2024; suppression remained incomplete and geometry-dependent.
why: Improves scintillation energy resolution and false-event rejection in photon-starved experiments.
key_works: Lee, Choong, and Cates (2024), [*Characterization of external optical crosstalk reduction for SiPM-based scintillation detectors with an optical bandpass filter*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nima.2024.169101).

title: Uncooled low-noise mid-infrared avalanche detector arrays
open: Extend low-excess-noise, high-gain mid-infrared avalanche detection toward room temperature while suppressing tunnelling and thermal dark currents across uniform, small-pixel focal-plane arrays.
status: A decades-old cooling constraint. Zhu demonstrated HgCdTe devices at 160 K in 2025 with gain approaching 189 and excess-noise factor below 1.4; uncooled arrays remain open.
why: Reduces cooling burden in sensitive thermal imaging and spectroscopy.
key_works: Zhu et al. (2025), [*High-temperature mid-wavelength infrared avalanche photodiode with modified fully-depleted absorption and multiplication region*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43246-025-00787-2).

title: Efficient mercury-free colloidal mid-infrared imaging arrays
open: Build uniform, stable, room-temperature 3–5-µm imaging arrays from mercury-, cadmium-, and lead-free colloidal semiconductors while retaining useful sensitivity, speed, and scalable deposition.
status: A 2020s challenge. Eom demonstrated Ag₂Te quantum-dot detection across 3–5 µm in 2026, measuring detectivity at 78 K; uncooled arrays require transport and noise improvements.
why: Supports solution-processed thermal imagers with different material supply and handling requirements.
key_works: Eom et al. (2026), [*Non-toxic silver telluride colloidal quantum dot mid-infrared photodetector*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-71374-3).

title: Experimental validation of low-noise multibarrier terahertz mixers
open: Demonstrate room-temperature InGaAs/InP multibarrier heterojunction mixers approaching predicted noise temperatures after including contacts, parasitics, antenna coupling, and realistic local-oscillator power and noise.
status: A newer extension of longstanding THz-receiver limits. Belio-Apaolaza and colleagues predicted intrinsic noise temperatures approaching ten times the quantum limit in 2025; this prediction requires experimental validation.
why: Could reduce refrigeration and oscillator-power requirements for coherent THz spectroscopy.
key_works: Belio-Apaolaza, Seddon, and Renaud (2025), [*Fermi-level-managed multi-barrier heterojunction diodes for terahertz detection*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-05299-0).

title: Predicting coupled chemical degradation in blue OLEDs
open: Predict blue OLED luminance decay and failure products from competing electron-, exciton-, and mixed-carrier reactions without individually fitting each device lifetime.
status: Open for decades. Kim combined calculations, control devices, and mass spectrometry in 2023 to identify electron-assisted degradation in iridium emitters; prediction across materials and conditions remains unresolved.
why: Guides durable emitter design beyond empirical lifetime screening.
key_works: Kim et al. (2023), [*Critical role of electrons in the short lifetime of blue OLEDs*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-43408-7).

title: High-brightness narrowband blue OLEDs without triplet accumulation
open: Maintain narrow deep-blue spectra and efficiency at sustained high brightness while suppressing trapping, triplet accumulation, annihilation, and chemical damage in sensitized emitters.
status: Pursued since the 2010s. Fan shifted molecular orbital energies in 2025, obtaining 13-nm emission bandwidth and approximately 20% efficiency at 1,000 cd/m²; high-brightness lifetime remains challenging.
why: Improves colour-pure, power-efficient displays under demanding luminance requirements.
key_works: Fan et al. (2025), [*Stable narrowband blue OLEDs by modulating frontier molecular orbital levels*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60172-y).

title: Efficient durable high-radiance near-infrared OLEDs
open: Combine high external efficiency, sustained near-infrared radiance, and long operational life at useful emitter area, overcoming nonradiative decay and annihilation without excessive heating.
status: Pursued since the 2000s. Liu and colleagues suppressed singlet–triplet annihilation in 2025, achieving 1.34% peak efficiency and exceptional current tolerance; measured lifetime still decreased sharply as operating current increased.
why: Enables compact organic illumination for spectroscopy and imaging.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), [*Ultrahigh-radiance near-infrared organic light-emitting diodes*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-025-01674-5).

title: Efficient hole injection into aluminium-rich deep-UV LEDs
open: Supply sufficient holes to high-aluminium-content AlGaN active regions without excessive resistive voltage, electron leakage, compensation, or degradation, particularly as emission moves below 250 nm.
status: A decades-old acceptor-activation problem. Liu improved 279-nm output 92.4% using periodic Mg doping in 2025; stronger aluminium enrichment retains difficult injection and contact constraints.
why: Improves electrical efficiency of compact deep-UV sources.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), [*Doping Engineering Strategy for Boosting the Performance of AlGaN-Based Deep-Ultraviolet Light-Emitting Diodes*](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.cgd.4c01612).

title: Deep-UV light extraction without absorbing contact losses
open: Efficiently extract ultraviolet photons while maintaining low-resistance hole contacts, uniform current spreading, and durability at useful power.
status: A longstanding trade-off. Hao combined micro-mesh contacts and scattering structures in 2025, obtaining 9.1% wall-plug efficiency at 275 nm and 12 mA; high-power durability remains open.
why: Reduces electricity and cooling requirements for ultraviolet sources.
key_works: Hao, Taniguchi, and Inoue (2025), [*Enhancement of wall-plug efficiency in AlGaN deep-ultraviolet light-emitting diodes by micro-mesh p-electrode and scattering nanostructures*](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0255184).

title: PFAS-free lithographic materials with equivalent process windows
open: Replace specific PFAS functions in resists, surfactants, and immersion coatings while preserving wetting, optical response, defectivity, and contamination compatibility under the same manufacturing conditions.
status: Substitution is active research; the 2025 GENESIS program includes PFAS-free photoresists. Replacing one formulation does not establish substitutions for every process function.
why: Reduces persistent chemical burdens without disrupting fabrication.
key_works: CEA-Leti/imec consortium (2025), [“GENESIS Project Launches to Lead Europe’s Transition To Sustainable Semiconductor Manufacturing”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/genesis-project-launches-lead-europes-transition-sustainable-semiconductor-manufacturing).

title: Low-climate-impact plasma chemistry for difficult etches
open: Replace high-impact etch and cleaning gases with chemistries that preserve profile, selectivity, particle control, and tool lifetime, assessing all reaction products rather than the feed gas alone.
status: Alternatives and process optimization exist; the 2024 plasma roadmap identifies sustainability and new chemistry as continuing technical challenges.
why: Reduces fabrication emissions at their source.
key_works: Oehrlein et al. (2024), [“Future of plasma etching for microelectronics: Challenges and opportunities”](https://doi.org/10.1116/6.0003579).

title: Complete fluorine mass balances around abatement
open: Measure transient inlet and outlet species, particles, liquid waste, and byproducts sufficiently well to verify actual destruction or recovery rather than displacement between waste streams.
status: Abatement systems and measurement protocols exist; GENESIS's 2025 program still targets sensor-integrated emissions monitoring and improved treatment.
why: Prevents nominal removal efficiency from concealing persistent or high-impact byproducts.
key_works: CEA-Leti/imec consortium (2025), [GENESIS project announcement](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/genesis-project-launches-lead-europes-transition-sustainable-semiconductor-manufacturing).

title: Closed-loop ultrapure water without impurity accumulation
open: Increase fab water recovery while preventing trace organics, ions, particles, and treatment byproducts from accumulating, including the energy and brine burden of the recovery loop.
status: Recycling and zero-liquid-discharge systems already exist; MAPT 2.0 identifies further purification, concentrating, and water–energy optimization needs.
why: Makes fabrication more resilient in water-stressed regions.
key_works: SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, “Sustainability & Energy Efficiency”](https://srcmapt.org/chapter2/).

title: Comparable lifecycle inventories per good die
open: Publish auditable energy, water, chemical, and emissions inventories normalized to yielding functional dies, including equipment utilization, process yield, packaging, and uncertainty.
status: Lifecycle frameworks and virtual-fab models exist; imec's 2025 account explicitly notes dependence on yield, utilization, die size, and other assumptions.
why: Allows meaningful comparison of fabrication routes and design choices.
key_works: imec (2025), [“How can we reduce environmental impact in chip manufacturing?”](https://www.imec-int.com/en/articles/how-can-we-reduce-environmental-impact-chip-manufacturing).

title: Affordable repeatable access to advanced pilot fabrication
open: Fund shared pilot capacity with predictable access, usable process baselines, and affordable repeated experiments for academic groups and small firms, including technologies unsuitable for production fabs.
status: Pilot-line initiatives are real; the 2025 NIST facilities announcement explicitly identifies shared 300 mm prototyping access as a gap. Announced facilities are not evidence of universal affordable access.
why: Lets promising devices accumulate the iteration and yield evidence needed for adoption.
key_works: NIST (2025), [announcement of the planned NSTC prototyping and NAPMP piloting facility](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/01/biden-harris-administration-announces-arizona-state-university-research).

title: Sustained maintenance and validation of open process kits
open: Establish recurring funding and ownership for open model calibration, rule corrections, regression tests, and silicon validation after initial PDK publication.
status: Open kits enable real test chips; SKY130's published documentation distinguishes its open release from production-qualified use. Release alone does not establish a sustainable validation service.
why: Keeps accessible design infrastructure trustworthy as tools and processes change.
key_works: SkyWater/Google (living documentation), [“Current Status—Experimental Preview”](https://skywater-pdk.readthedocs.io/en/main/status.html).

title: Supply-chain dependency maps that reveal substitutability
open: Map critical materials, equipment subcomponents, process qualifications, and actual substitute lead times across supplier tiers while protecting confidential commercial data.
status: OECD's 2025 mapping identifies concentrations and datasets but frames dependency and vulnerability identification as continuing work; trade totals alone cannot describe qualification bottlenecks.
why: Makes resilience investments address genuine single points of failure.
key_works: OECD (2025), [“Mapping the semiconductor value chain: Working towards identifying dependencies and vulnerabilities”](https://doi.org/10.1787/4154cdbf-en).

title: Hands-on semiconductor workforce capacity beyond major clusters
open: Fund geographically accessible equipment, instructors, and paid training pathways, and measure whether they fill specific process, maintenance, packaging, and metrology skill gaps over economic cycles.
status: MAPT 2.0 identifies imprecise workforce data, concentrated training infrastructure, and an imbalance between capital and workforce investment.
why: Prevents equipment and research investment from being stranded by missing practical expertise.
key_works: SRC (2025), [MAPT 2.0, “Workforce Development”](https://srcmapt.org/chapter11/).

title: Semiconductor-grade recovery of critical process materials
open: Recover useful materials from dilute mixed fab wastes and return them to qualified process use, demonstrating impurity control, net environmental benefit, and economic viability.
status: Recycling works for selected streams; GENESIS's 2025 program includes raw-material reuse and critical-material mitigation, leaving many material–waste-stream combinations unresolved.
why: Reduces dependence on concentrated primary supplies and lowers waste.
key_works: CEA-Leti/imec consortium (2025), [GENESIS project announcement](https://www.imec-int.com/en/press/genesis-project-launches-lead-europes-transition-sustainable-semiconductor-manufacturing).

title: Predictive charged-defect energetics
open: Predict defect formation free energies and charge-transition levels with transferable uncertainty estimates, including localized states, competing geometries, and realistic chemical potentials. Success requires blind agreement with independently identified defects across semiconductor families.
status: A decades-old problem; finite-size corrections and hybrid functionals substantially improved calculations, but defect-specific validation remains necessary.
why: Makes doping and carrier-lifetime engineering less empirical.
key_works: C. Freysoldt et al. (2014), [First-principles calculations for point defects in solids](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.253).

title: Multimode anharmonic nonradiative capture
open: Calculate defect capture rates when multiple vibrational modes, anharmonicity, tunnelling, and strong electronic coupling act simultaneously. Establish experimentally validated criteria for when single-coordinate approximations fail.
status: Decades old; 2014 calculations quantitatively described selected GaN and ZnO defects, leaving broader multimode and anharmonic cases unresolved.
why: Identifies which rare defects actually dominate recombination.
key_works: A. Alkauskas, Q. Yan, and C. G. Van de Walle (2014), [First-principles theory of nonradiative carrier capture via multiphonon emission](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.90.075202).

title: Excited-state defect recombination networks
open: Predict recombination through a defect’s complete network of charge states, metastable geometries, and electronic excited states under injection. Determine which pathways dominate as temperature and carrier density change.
status: Excited-state contributions were established in 2016; validated networks across different defects and operating conditions remain incomplete.
why: Ground-state-only screening can misidentify dangerous defects.
key_works: A. Alkauskas et al. (2016), [Role of excited states in Shockley-Read-Hall recombination in wide-band-gap semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.93.201304).

title: Auger–Meitner rates in realistic indirect-gap materials
open: Predict Auger–Meitner recombination with phonon assistance, strain, alloy disorder, screening, and carrier degeneracy, without independently fitting every sample. Experimentally separate the competing microscopic channels.
status: Longstanding; a consistent first-principles treatment of direct and phonon-assisted silicon recombination appeared in 2023.
why: Determines intrinsic carrier-density and efficiency limits.
key_works: K. Bushick and E. Kioupakis (2023), [Phonon-Assisted Auger-Meitner Recombination in Silicon from First Principles](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.076902).

title: Finite-density polaron transport across coupling regimes
open: Connect coherent band transport and activated polaron hopping at finite carrier density, including disorder and carrier interactions. Reproduce conductivity spectra and mobility using the same microscopic parameters.
status: Decades old; realistic first-principles diagrammatic Monte Carlo calculations appeared in 2025, while dense interacting transport remains harder.
why: Improves predictions for oxide, organic, and soft-lattice semiconductors.
key_works: Y. Luo, J. Park, and M. Bernardi (2025), [First-principles diagrammatic Monte Carlo for electron–phonon interactions and polaron](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-025-02954-1).

title: Mobility beyond phonon quasiparticles
open: Predict carrier mobility in strongly anharmonic semiconductors at dilute doping, including quantum nuclei and impurity scattering. Establish convergence and uncertainty with respect to simulation size and duration.
status: Decades old; a 2024 molecular-dynamics/Kubo–Greenwood approach incorporates nonperturbative anharmonic coupling, but realistic dilute impurities remain difficult.
why: Extends transport prediction beyond well-defined quasiparticles.
key_works: J. Quan, C. Carbogno, and M. Scheffler (2024), [Carrier mobility of strongly anharmonic materials from first principles](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.110.235202).

title: Spatial hot-phonon bottleneck inversion
open: Infer local carrier and phonon distributions without confusing transport with changing spectra. Predict when phonon reabsorption produces expanding, contracting, or non-Gaussian carrier profiles.
status: Longstanding; 2024 MoS₂ microscopy resolved expansion, apparent negative diffusion, and subsequent expansion, leaving transferable microscopic inversion open.
why: Replaces misleading single-temperature descriptions of energy flow.
key_works: X. Wei et al. (2024), [Unveiling Spatiotemporal Diffusion of Hot Carriers Influenced by Spatial Nonuniform Hot Phonon Bottleneck Effect in Monolayer MoS2](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c02059).

title: Atomic dislocation cores to recombination lifetimes
open: Predict dislocation recombination activity from reconstructed cores, impurity decoration, charge, and motion. Connect atomistic rates to measured lifetimes across realistic dislocation networks.
status: Debated for decades; first-principles screw-dislocation carrier dynamics appeared in 2025, while decorated and interacting cores remain incompletely characterized.
why: Dislocation density alone cannot predict electrical quality.
key_works: Q. Gao et al. (2025), [First principles calculations of carrier dynamics of screw dislocation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-025-01533-5).

title: Kinetic dopability limits
open: Bound achievable free-carrier concentrations when incorporation, compensation, metastability, and relaxation compete. Distinguish equilibrium prohibitions from kinetically accessible states.
status: Decades old; a 2024 review identifies conductivity control as a central ultrawide-gap barrier.
why: Identifies chemically feasible doping strategies.
key_works: J. L. Lyons, D. Wickramaratne, and A. Janotti (2024), [Dopants and defects in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cossms.2024.101148).

title: The Ta2NiSe5 excitonic order parameter
open: Establish whether electron–hole pairing drives the Ta₂NiSe₅ transition, follows lattice distortion, or forms inseparable cooperative order. A decisive experiment must distinguish these possibilities beyond observing a gap.
status: The excitonic-insulator proposal dates to the 1960s; 2025 measurements still address competing electronic and lattice interpretations.
why: Establishes when excitonic insulation is a distinct thermodynamic phase.
key_works: N. Maraytta et al. (2025), [Unveiling excitonic insulator signatures in Ta2NiSe5 through structural and orbital probes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-20909-7).

title: Universality of the doped-semiconductor metal–insulator transition
open: Explain transport, magnetic susceptibility, and rare-region behavior near the transition in compensated and uncompensated materials within one testable theory. Separate universal exponents from crossover and disorder effects.
status: Open since mid-twentieth-century localization research; a 2023 synthesis connects random singlets, Kondo physics, and multifractality while identifying remaining problems.
why: Doped silicon provides a controlled test of interacting localization.
key_works: S. Kettemann (2023), [Towards a Comprehensive Theory of Metal-Insulator Transitions in Doped Semiconductors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02932).

title: Carrier-mediated ferromagnetism in dilute wide-gap nitrides
open: Demonstrate homogeneous dilute magnetic nitrides with reproducible, carrier-controlled ferromagnetism above room temperature, excluding precipitates and secondary phases. Establish the exchange mechanism using complementary probes.
status: Pursued since around 2000; established low-temperature functionalities do not establish this combined high-temperature target.
why: Connects electrical carrier control with robust magnetic functionality.
key_works: T. Dietl and H. Ohno (2014), [Dilute ferromagnetic semiconductors: Physics and spintronic structures](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.86.187); [arXiv:1307.3429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3429).

title: Exciton–plasma transition away from optical equilibrium
open: Determine the order, critical scaling, and equation of state of exciton ionization when generation, recombination, disorder, and screening compete. Establish which equilibrium Mott-transition concepts survive finite lifetimes.
status: Longstanding; black-phosphorus experiments reported critical scaling and a density–temperature diagram in 2022.
why: Makes dense-carrier optical and transport responses predictable.
key_works: B. Zheng et al. (2022), [Quantum criticality of excitonic Mott metal-insulator transitions in black phosphorus](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35567-w).

title: Thermalization of moiré exciton Mott states
open: Establish coherence, thermalization, and relaxation pathways of interacting moiré excitons under pumping and finite lifetime. Distinguish kinetic arrest from equilibrium insulating order.
status: A 2020s problem; 2025 experiments found frozen motion lasting over 70 ns, leaving longer-time and driven steady-state dynamics open.
why: Tests whether exciton lattices realize controlled interacting phases.
key_works: S. Deng et al. (2025), [Frozen non-equilibrium dynamics of exciton Mott insulators in moiré superlattices](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-025-02135-8).

title: Complete basal-plane-dislocation conversion
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Convert inherited basal-plane dislocations into benign configurations throughout thick 4H-SiC epitaxy without creating new active defects. Demonstrate reproducibility across wafers and growth histories.
status: Pursued for decades; epitaxial conversion has improved, but a 2025 review retains nucleation, propagation, and conversion control as active challenges.
why: Residual defects can initiate current-driven degradation.
key_works: Y. Li et al. (2025), [Dislocations in 4H-SiC epilayers for power devices: Identification, formation, and regulation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mssp.2024.109147).

title: Injection-stable SiC stacking faults
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Prevent recombination-enhanced stacking-fault expansion across high injection, temperature cycling, and long service without sacrificing lifetime or blocking performance.
status: Decades old; selected implantation conditions produced zero expansion density in 2025. Broader operating-envelope validation remains open.
why: Enables stable high-current bipolar SiC devices.
key_works: M. Kato et al. (2025), [Suppression of the Degradation in SiC Power Devices using High-energy Ion Implantation](https://doi.org/10.11470/jsaprev.250424).

title: SiC/SiO2 near-interface trap identity
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Assign electrically active near-interface traps to atomic structures and connect each population to mobility and trapping. Remove them without introducing compensating reliability penalties.
status: Decades old; passivation improves interfaces, but the 2025 assessment still identifies active defects as a principal limitation.
why: Enables mechanism-based interface treatments.
key_works: L. Luo and Y. Zhong (2025), [The Principles and Applications of Electrical Characterization Techniques for Electrically Active Defects in 4H-SiC Devices](https://doi.org/10.1002/pssa.202400840).

title: Spatially selective SiC lifetime control
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Independently engineer minority-carrier lifetime across device regions while preserving leakage and blocking stability. Predict the evolution of intentionally introduced defects during operation.
status: Decades of lifetime-control experiments exist; 2025 reviews retain lifetime-limiting defects as material constraints.
why: Different regions require different conduction–switching compromises.
key_works: I. Capan (2025), [Electrically Active Defects in 3C, 4H, and 6H Silicon Carbide Polytypes: A Review](https://doi.org/10.3390/cryst15030255).

title: SiC threshold drift over realistic mission profiles
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Predict reversible and permanent threshold shifts under arbitrary temperature, gate-bias, and switching histories from identifiable trap populations.
status: Prominent since the 2010s; reliability models still transfer imperfectly between stress protocols.
why: Supports dependable protection margins.
key_works: T. Avraham, M. Dhyani, and J. B. Bernstein (2025), [Reliability Challenges, Models, and Physics of Silicon Carbide and Gallium Nitride Power Devices](https://doi.org/10.3390/en18051046).

title: SiC short-circuit ruggedness without efficiency loss
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Increase short-circuit survival while preserving efficiency and current density; quantitatively resolve localized heating, oxide stress, and parasitic conduction.
status: Longstanding; the 2025 review identifies unresolved ruggedness–performance trade-offs.
why: Makes efficient converters tolerate faults.
key_works: T. Avraham, M. Dhyani, and J. B. Bernstein (2025), [Reliability Challenges, Models, and Physics of Silicon Carbide and Gallium Nitride Power Devices](https://doi.org/10.3390/en18051046).

title: Low-defect 3C-SiC on silicon
subfield: Silicon carbide materials and power physics
open: Grow thick cubic SiC on silicon with jointly suppressed stacking faults, antiphase boundaries, voids, and wafer bow. Demonstrate reproducible low-leakage electrical material.
status: Studied for over thirty years; 2021 microscopy clarified defect structures without eliminating the combined mismatch problem.
why: Could provide lower-cost large-area wide-gap substrates.
key_works: M. Zimbone et al. (2021), [Extended defects in 3C-SiC: Stacking faults, threading partial dislocations, and inverted domain boundaries](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.actamat.2021.116915).

title: Affordable native GaN substrates
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Produce larger native GaN wafers with low defect density, controlled conductivity, and usable yield at costs supporting widespread vertical devices.
status: Commercial substrates exist; cost and quality barriers persist from the 2018 roadmap into a 2026 assessment.
why: Reduces defects and mismatch in vertical structures.
key_works: H. Amano et al. (2018), [The 2018 GaN power electronics roadmap](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6463/aaaf9d); R. Shankari et al. (2026), [Vertical gallium nitride MOSFETs: Advanced architectures, fabrication technologies, and performance breakthroughs for high-power applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mee.2025.112418).

title: Selective implanted p-type GaN
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Form selective p-type regions by implantation with high activation, limited compensation, repaired damage, and preserved junction quality.
status: A persistent obstacle since early GaN power-device development; activation demonstrations have not established broadly manufacturable processing.
why: Enables junction isolation and vertical bipolar structures.
key_works: H. Amano et al. (2018), [The 2018 GaN power electronics roadmap](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6463/aaaf9d).

title: Repetitive avalanche in vertical GaN
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Sustain repeated high-current avalanche with predictable energy limits, stable termination, and negligible cumulative trap generation.
status: Avalanche-capable junctions and kilovolt devices exist; the 2026 assessment retains integration and reliability barriers.
why: Enables robust overvoltage survival.
key_works: R. Shankari et al. (2026), [Vertical gallium nitride MOSFETs: Advanced architectures, fabrication technologies, and performance breakthroughs for high-power applications](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mee.2025.112418).

title: Multi-kilovolt GaN current collapse
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Suppress trapping-induced dynamic resistance at multi-kilovolt stress without sacrificing blocking voltage, leakage, or switching speed.
status: Longstanding; a 2026 review reports progress through 960 V stress while retaining higher-voltage suppression as difficult.
why: Reduces actual switching losses.
key_works: J. Yang et al. (2026), [Dynamic instabilities in GaN power devices: mechanisms, challenges and advancements](https://doi.org/10.35848/1347-4065/ae2d61).

title: GaN dynamic threshold stability
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Stabilize threshold voltage through fast bipolar gate excursions while preserving normally-off margins and gate robustness.
status: A prominent 2010s–2020s problem; the 2026 review retains coupled injection, trapping, and recovery challenges.
why: Preserves switching and protection margins.
key_works: J. Yang et al. (2026), [Dynamic instabilities in GaN power devices: mechanisms, challenges and advancements](https://doi.org/10.35848/1347-4065/ae2d61).

title: Millimeter-wave GaN hot-electron degradation
subfield: Gallium nitride power and radio-frequency materials
open: Predict degradation from hot electrons, field crowding, chemistry, and electromechanical stress in short-gate GaN. Validate accelerated-test extrapolation against realistic modulated signals.
status: Studied for decades; the 2022 review retains simultaneous control of dispersion, short-channel effects, and hot-electron damage as difficult.
why: Preserves RF gain and efficiency throughout service.
key_works: E. Zanoni et al. (2022), [Failure Physics and Reliability of GaN-Based HEMTs for Microwave and Millimeter-Wave Applications: A Review of Consolidated Data and Recent Results](https://doi.org/10.1002/pssa.202100722).

title: Useful p-type beta-Ga2O3
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Demonstrate reproducible mobile-hole transport with useful density and mobility, or establish practical self-trapping and compensation limits.
status: Longstanding; the 2024 review establishes no useful bipolar conductivity.
why: Enables native p–n junction functionality.
key_works: J. L. Lyons, D. Wickramaratne, and A. Janotti (2024), [Dopants and defects in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cossms.2024.101148).

title: Intrinsic electrothermal limits of Ga2O3
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Establish validated continuous-operation limits when anisotropic thermal transport, hot carriers, and temperature-dependent losses interact. Identify geometries exploiting high field strength without thermal runaway.
status: Identified throughout the 2010s; pulsed electrical records and selected cooling demonstrations do not establish continuous-operation limits.
why: Determines which power applications benefit from Ga₂O₃.
key_works: S. J. Pearton et al. (2018), [A review of Ga2O3 materials, processing, and devices](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5006941).

title: Atomic assignment of electrically active Ga2O3 defects
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Assign measured trap families to vacancies, impurities, complexes, and local structures, including charge states and capture cross-sections. Reconcile spectroscopy, calculations, growth chemistry, and irradiation.
status: Active since electronic-grade Ga₂O₃ emerged; McCluskey’s 2020 tutorial documents both established behavior and incomplete assignments.
why: Enables reproducible compensation and leakage control.
key_works: M. D. McCluskey (2020), [Point defects in Ga2O3](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5142195); [author publication list](https://labs.wsu.edu/mccluskey/publications/articles2020/).

title: Controlled Ga2O3 polymorph conversion
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Select and retain a desired polymorph through growth, implantation, annealing, and electrical stress. Determine kinetic pathways and stability windows beyond zero-temperature energy ordering.
status: Active throughout the 2020s; 2024 atomic-resolution experiments resolved gamma/beta transformations.
why: Enables new symmetries while avoiding hidden phase-related failures.
key_works: J. García-Fernández et al. (2024), [In situ atomic-resolution study of transformations in double polymorph gamma/beta-Ga2O3 structures](https://doi.org/10.1039/D3MA01011B).

title: High-density high-mobility AlGaO/Ga2O3 channels
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Sustain high sheet density and mobility while controlling alloy disorder, compensation, roughness, and parallel conduction in modulation-doped oxide heterostructures.
status: Modulation doping was demonstrated in 2017; 2024 research retains composition-dependent donor and compensation constraints.
why: Improves oxide RF and high-current transport.
key_works: S. Krishnamoorthy et al. (2017), [Modulation-doped beta-(Al0.2Ga0.8)2O3/Ga2O3 field-effect transistor](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4993569); F. Tuomisto (2024), [Defects and doping in ultra-wide band gap (Al,Ga)N and beta-(Al,Ga)2O3 alloys](https://doi.org/10.1557/s43578-024-01407-4).

title: Repetitive avalanche and surge in oxide heterojunctions
subfield: Gallium oxide and related ultrawide-gap oxides
open: Demonstrate repeated avalanche and surge survival over temperature and ageing, with stable interfaces and measured degradation distributions as area and voltage increase.
status: NiO/Ga₂O₃ junctions achieved avalanche and surge currents above 50 A in 2023.
why: Establishes practical converter fault tolerance.
key_works: F. Zhou et al. (2023), [An avalanche-and-surge robust ultrawide-bandgap heterojunction for power electronics](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-40194-0).

title: Room-temperature electron conduction in doped diamond
open: Obtain useful, reproducible room-temperature electron density and mobility with low compensation and stable dopant profiles.
status: Pursued for decades; 2024 n-channel devices reached approximately 150 cm²/V·s at 573 K.
why: Enables broader bipolar diamond electronics.
key_works: Liao et al. (2024), [High-Temperature and High-Electron Mobility Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors Based on N-Type Diamond](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202306013).

title: Large-area electronic-grade diamond growth
open: Increase growth rate and usable single-crystal area while preserving impurity uniformity, low dislocation density, thickness control, and electronic-grade yield.
status: Longstanding; 2024 work reports nitrogen-free growth above 250 µm/h while retaining area scaling as a challenge.
why: Determines economically usable diamond device area.
key_works: K. Ichikawa et al. (2024), [Diamond Homoepitaxial Growth Technology toward Wafer Fabrication, Atomically Controlled Surfaces, and Low Resistivity](https://doi.org/10.1021/accountsmr.4c00123).

title: Environment-independent diamond surface transfer doping
open: Maintain controlled surface-hole density under humidity, vacuum, temperature cycling, and electrical stress using stable charge-transfer chemistry.
status: Atmospheric transfer doping was established in 2000; modern diamond development retains interface-stability challenges.
why: Makes surface-conducting devices environmentally predictable.
key_works: F. Maier et al. (2000), [Origin of Surface Conductivity in Diamond](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.3472); D. Eon (2024), [Diamonds in the Current: Navigating Challenges for the Integration of Diamond in Power Electronics](https://doi.org/10.1002/pssa.202400085).

title: Stable low-resistance contacts to n-type diamond
open: Produce uniform electron-injecting contacts surviving high temperature and current, while separating contact barriers from bulk donor freeze-out.
status: Decades old; elevated-temperature n-channel demonstrations leave substantial injection and bulk-resistance constraints.
why: Prevents contacts from dominating power losses.
key_works: Liao et al. (2024), [High-Temperature and High-Electron Mobility Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors Based on N-Type Diamond](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202306013).

title: Diamond impact-ionization coefficients
open: Measure electron and hole ionization coefficients across orientation, temperature, and field, distinguishing intrinsic avalanche from defect-assisted or contact-limited breakdown.
status: Longstanding uncertainty; 2024 first-principles simulations agreed with available hole data, leaving comprehensive validation of both carriers incomplete.
why: Supports defensible diamond voltage limits.
key_works: J. Shoemaker et al. (2024), [First-principles modeling of high-field transport in diamond](https://experts.azregents.edu/en/publications/first-principles-modeling-of-high-field-transport-in-diamond/).

title: Efficient bulk p-type AlN
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Achieve reproducible bulk hole conduction with adequate activation, low compensation, and preserved crystal quality. Identify the actual transport mechanism.
status: Pursued for decades; a 2024 review describes renewed Be-doping progress alongside incorporation, acceptor-depth, and solubility constraints.
why: Enables bipolar ultrawide-gap nitride structures.
key_works: T. Wostatek et al. (2024), [Ammonothermal Crystal Growth of Functional Nitrides for Semiconductor Devices: Status and Potential](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17133104).

title: Stable shallow donors in AlN
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Experimentally establish a reproducible shallow-donor mechanism surviving processing and operation. Test whether predicted metastable configurations can be populated without compensating defects.
status: Decades old; 2026 calculations predict overlooked metastable aluminum-interstitial shallow donors.
why: Addresses severe donor freeze-out.
key_works: Y. Liu, S. Chae, and E. Kioupakis (2026), [Origin of shallow n-type doping in AlN](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-026-02192-w).

title: Uniform large-diameter AlN single crystals
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Scale sublimation growth while jointly controlling impurities, stress, dislocations, cracking, and wafer yield. Validate coupled growth models using spatially resolved measurements.
status: Decades of development; a 2025 review reports progress toward 2–4-inch crystals while retaining diameter and quality constraints.
why: Enables economically useful ultrawide-gap substrate areas.
key_works: W. Li et al. (2025), [Recent Advances in PVT Growth of Large-Diameter, High-Quality Aluminum Nitride Single Crystals](https://doi.org/10.1002/crat.202500038).

title: Compensation-controlled cubic-BN doping
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Control shallow n- and p-type doping while suppressing compensating defects and complexes; demonstrate reproducible bulk transport.
status: Junction demonstrations date to the 1990s; 2022 calculations identify persistent compensation barriers.
why: Enables extreme-temperature bipolar devices.
key_works: T. Joshi et al. (2022), [Doping limitations of cubic boron nitride: Effects of unintentional defects on shallow doping](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.054101).

title: Thick phase-pure cubic-BN epitaxy
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Grow thick, large-area cubic BN without destructive stress, delamination, or noncubic inclusions while preserving electronic quality.
status: Deposition has advanced for decades; high-quality synthesis remains a prerequisite highlighted in 2022.
why: Enables reproducible high-voltage structures.
key_works: T. Joshi et al. (2022), [Doping limitations of cubic boron nitride: Effects of unintentional defects on shallow doping](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.054101).

title: Bulk n-type hexagonal BN
subfield: Aluminum nitride and boron nitride semiconductors
open: Translate shallow-donor concepts into stable multilayer or bulk hBN electron transport with useful current density. Resolve compensation and anisotropic conduction.
status: A 2022 Ge–O study demonstrated monolayer n-type transport and a rectifying heterojunction; bulk conductivity remains distinct.
why: Enables thicker ultrawide-gap junctions and radiation sensors.
key_works: S. Lu et al. (2022), [Towards n-type conductivity in hexagonal boron nitride](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-30762-1).

title: Long-life Mg3Sb2 without magnesium loss
open: Preserve Mg₃(Sb,Bi)₂ composition, carrier density, and thermoelectric performance through prolonged heating and cycling without transport penalties from diffusion barriers.
status: A 2010s–2020s problem; Ga-rich grain-boundary complexions enabled substantial stabilization and seven-day device testing in 2026.
why: Prevents service-life drift of thermoelectric output.
key_works: Y. Geng et al. (2026), [Grain boundary complexions stabilize Mg3Sb2-based thermoelectric devices with superior performance](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2026.102443).

title: Reproducible cycling-stable SnSe thermoelectrics
open: Establish cross-laboratory synthesis and measurement protocols producing reproducible polycrystalline SnSe performance through repeated heating. Resolve stoichiometry, mobile defects, and sample-history effects.
status: Recurrent since the 2010s; a 2025 study reached ZT 1.04 at 873 K but degraded after cycling and annealing.
why: Makes lifetime performance comparable between laboratories.
key_works: M. Thiem et al. (2025), [Stability of SnSe-Based Thermoelectric Compounds](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma18184228).

title: Suppressing bipolar heat conduction without losing power factor
open: Suppress minority-carrier excitation while preserving majority-carrier mobility and Seebeck coefficient. Predict the combined effects of bandgap, Fermi level, and scattering.
status: Longstanding; 2024 measurements showed Burstein–Moss-related suppression despite bandgap narrowing.
why: Preserves high-temperature thermoelectric efficiency.
key_works: C. Zhao et al. (2024), [Burstein-moss effect leads to an unusual suppression of bipolar conduction with shrinking bandgap](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4TA04110K).

title: Durable high-performance n-type organic thermoelectrics
open: Combine efficient electron doping, high power factor, low thermal conductivity, and air stability in solution-processable materials surviving thermal and mechanical cycling.
status: Pursued since the 2000s; a 2025 assessment retains linked doping-efficiency and stability barriers.
why: Enables balanced, durable flexible thermoelectric modules.
key_works: H. Li et al. (2025), [Side-chain engineering of conjugated molecules for n-type organic thermoelectrics](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5MH00067J).

title: Fatigue-resistant plastic inorganic thermoelectrics
open: Preserve thermoelectric efficiency under repeated tensile and bending strain. Determine how plasticity-enabling dislocations affect transport and accumulated damage.
status: Rapid progress since 2018; a 2024 Mg-based material combined approximately 43% strain with room-temperature ZT around 0.72.
why: Enables durable conformal heat harvesting.
key_works: A. Li et al. (2024), [High performance magnesium-based plastic semiconductors for flexible thermoelectrics](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-49440-5).

title: Polarization-free high-flux CdZnTe
open: Maintain uniform fields, stable collection, and low leakage in thick CdZnTe under intense irradiation. Control both bias-induced and radiation-induced trap charging over large areas.
status: Studied for decades; high-flux material and 2024 XIDer experiments improve performance, but trapping and time-dependent leakage persist.
why: Enables detectors for intense next-generation light sources.
key_works: M. Collonge et al. (2024), [Probing the potential of CdZnTe for high-energy high-flux 2D X-ray detection using the XIDer incremental digital integrating readout](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphy.2024.1304570).

title: Long-duration perovskite X-ray baseline stability
open: Suppress ionic redistribution and electrode reactions during prolonged biased irradiation while retaining sensitivity and spatial uniformity. Bound drift across dose histories and manufacturing lots.
status: Central since the 2010s; 2024 CsPbBr₃ growth demonstrated low drift and thirty-day stability.
why: Prevents baseline changes from obscuring radiation signals.
key_works: Y. Hua et al. (2024), [Suppressed ion migration for high-performance X-ray detectors based on atmosphere-controlled EFG-grown perovskite CsPbBr3 single crystals](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-024-01480-5).

title: Radiation-damage evolution in SiC detectors
open: Predict collection loss, polarization, and recovery under mixed radiation fields across temperature, dose rate, and annealing history. Identify the controlling defect complexes.
status: Studied for decades; a 2024 irradiation experiment measured collection decline from 100% to 90.8% under its conditions.
why: Quantifies radiation tolerance for actual environments.
key_works: Z. Long et al. (2024), [Neutron irradiation and polarization effect of 4H-SiC Schottky detector](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nima.2024.169326).

title: Efficient thick hBN fast-neutron detection
open: Increase fast-neutron conversion and charge collection while preserving gamma rejection, low dark current, and useful detector area.
status: A growing 2010s–2020s field; 2025 millimeter-thick devices reported 0.7% AmBe and 0.5% Cf-252 efficiency, with approximately 38% charge collection.
why: Enables compact semiconductor alternatives to bulky neutron detectors.
key_works: G. Somasundaram et al. (2025), [Development of millimeter-thick hexagonal boron nitride wafers and fast neutron detectors](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0274262).

title: Impurity-limited high-purity germanium scaling
open: Grow larger detector-grade volumes while controlling impurity segregation and trapping throughout the boule. Connect identified defects to measured charge losses.
status: Pursued for decades; 2025 calculations clarified group-V impurity energetics, while consistent large-volume performance remains difficult.
why: Supplies reproducible detector mass for rare-event searches.
key_works: S. Aryal, E. R. Batista, and G. Wang (2025), [First-Principles insights into group-V impurities and their impact on germanium detector performance](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-25057-6).

title: Sub-keV nuclear-recoil ionization yield
open: Measure and explain electron–hole production distributions from low-energy Si and Ge nuclear recoils, including thresholds and crystal orientation. Resolve conflicting measurements using traceable recoil calibration.
status: Decades old; a 2024 Ge experiment revisited 254 eV recoils after inconsistent earlier yields.
why: Controls interpretations of neutrino and light-dark-matter searches.
key_works: A. R. L. Kavner and I. Jovanovic (2024), [Measurement of ionization produced by 254 eV nuclear recoils in germanium](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.083043).

title: Mixed ion–electron transport beyond one polymer
open: Predict coupled ionic and electronic motion across materials, electrolytes, and hydration states, incorporating chemical potentials, swelling, and disorder.
status: Longstanding; a 2023 model reproduced selected PEDOT:PSS kinetics, leaving transfer across chemistries and dynamic morphologies open.
why: Improves prediction of electrochemical transistor transients.
key_works: S. T. Keene, A. Rao, and G. G. Malliaras (2023), [The relationship between ionic-electronic coupling and transport in organic mixed conductors](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adi3536).

title: Oxidative lifetime of organic electrochemical channels
open: Retain transconductance, threshold, and reversible charge capacity during prolonged cycling in oxygenated water. Separate useful trap filling from irreversible oxidation.
status: Longstanding; controlled chemical doping improved n- and p-type stability in 2025.
why: Enables stable amplification in physiological environments.
key_works: V. N. Le et al. (2025), [Improved organic electrochemical transistor stability using solvent degassing and chemical doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-024-01297-8).

title: Chronic semiconductor–tissue interface stability
open: Maintain transduction and low-impedance tissue coupling through long implantation without progressive inflammation, delamination, or drift. Evaluate electronics together with the evolving biological response.
status: Decades old; a 2026 review documents compliance and integration advances while retaining chronic stability and foreign-body-response obstacles.
why: Enables dependable long-term physiological interfaces.
key_works: R. Bai, Z. Zhao, and F. Yan (2026), [Organic Electrochemical Transistors in Tissue-Interfaced Bioelectronics](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202513422).

title: Cyclic-strain reliability of stretchable semiconductors
open: Preserve mobility, threshold uniformity, and noise under repeated multidirectional stretching, creep, humidity, and ageing. Identify electrical damage before visible fracture.
status: Rapid progress since the 2010s; 2024 devices exceeded 20 cm²/V·s average mobility under 100% strain.
why: Makes deformable electronics predictable throughout use.
key_works: D. Zhong et al. (2024), [High-speed and large-scale intrinsically stretchable integrated circuits](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07096-7).

title: Reproducible electronic-grade conjugated-polymer synthesis
open: Control molecular weight, sequence defects, end groups, and catalyst residues while preserving batch-level electrical performance. Establish chemical specifications predictive of device behavior.
status: Decades old; 2024 room-temperature Suzuki–Miyaura chemistry covered 24 conjugated polymers, leaving production reproducibility across chemistries open.
why: Prevents nominally identical polymers from behaving differently.
key_works: H. Xiong et al. (2024), [General room-temperature Suzuki–Miyaura polymerization for organic electronics](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-023-01794-9).

title: Fast Czochralski growth without transient vacancy voids
subfield: Bulk silicon crystal and wafer engineering
open: Maintain vacancy-void size and density below declared limits through the entire ingot without sacrificing pulling throughput. Validate control across furnaces and feedstock histories.
status: Decades old; a 2025 coupled model explained reduced crystal-originated particles with a cooling tube.
why: Reduces wafer rejection and device-killing crystalline defects.
key_works: S.-K. Yang and A. R. Ansari Dezfoli (2025), [Multiscale modeling of COP suppression in Czochralski grown Silicon: Insights into cooling tube effects](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mssp.2025.109923).

title: Shorter anneals for internally gettered heavily doped silicon
subfield: Bulk silicon crystal and wafer engineering
open: Proposed target: reduce high-temperature holding time tenfold while preserving a deep precipitate-free surface region and effective bulk gettering in heavily boron-doped silicon.
status: Decades of optimization; a 2026 study achieved denuded zones exceeding 40 µm using rapid annealing plus three hours at 1200 °C.
why: Lowers substrate processing cost and energy.
key_works: J. Wang et al. (2026), [Engineering oxygen precipitation for simultaneous denuded zone and bulk microdefect formation in pre-annealed heavily boron-doped Czochralski silicon substrates for p/p+ epitaxial wafers](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mssp.2025.110118).

title: Resistivity homogeneity in large float-zone silicon
subfield: Bulk silicon crystal and wafer engineering
open: Bound radial and axial resistivity variation in 200-mm float-zone silicon while preserving zone stability and throughput. Predict rotation schedules using validated three-dimensional flow and segregation models.
status: Diameter scaling has challenged growth for decades; alternating rotation improved radial distributions in 2024.
why: Improves high-voltage device and detector uniformity.
key_works: D. Yan et al. (2024), [Effect of Crystal Rotation on Melt Convection and Resistivity Distribution in 200 mm Floating Zone Silicon Single Crystal Growth](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.4c05573).

title: Seamless single-domain crystallization at wafer dimensions
open: Scale seed-controlled MoS₂ crystallization to production wafers with reproducible monolayer coverage and verified absence of translational coalescence boundaries.
status: A 2010s–2020s problem; two-dimensional Czochralski growth produced centimetre-scale single domains in 2025.
why: Eliminates circuit dependence on growth-boundary placement.
key_works: H. Jiang et al. (2025), [Two-dimensional Czochralski growth of single-crystal MoS2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-024-02069-7).

title: Repeatable wafer transfer with bounded rare damage
open: Transfer semiconductor monolayers with reproducible bounds on cracks, wrinkles, contamination, and residual strain across lots and increasing wafer diameters.
status: Transfer damage has limited integration since the 2010s; four-inch oxide-mediated dry transfer was demonstrated in 2026.
why: Converts local material quality into large-area yield.
key_works: X. Xu et al. (2026), [Wafer-scale integration of single-crystalline molybdenum disulfide for flexible electronics using oxide dry transfer](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-026-01598-0).

title: Nonmonotonic illumination drift in flexible IGZO
open: Predict and suppress threshold-drift reversal under combined negative bias, illumination, and heating. Transfer the model across thicknesses, spectra, and display duty cycles.
status: A longstanding oxide-backplane problem; 2025 work linked reversal to hydrogen/oxygen-associated states and suppressed it through thickness optimization.
why: Prevents brightness drift during low-refresh operation.
key_works: D. Kim, K.-B. Lee, and B. Choi (2025), [Hydrogen and oxygen induced abnormal reliability degradation in flexible top-gate amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O thin-film transistors under negative bias thermal illumination stress](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mejo.2025.106902).

title: Display-grade p-type oxide transistor uniformity
open: Produce panel-uniform p-type SnO transistors combining mobility, low leakage, and lifetime stability in processes compatible with n-type oxide drivers.
status: The p-type gap dates to the 2000s; Tm-doped SnO reached 12.8 cm²/V·s and working complementary gates in 2025.
why: Enables complementary circuitry directly on display glass.
key_works: J. Han et al. (2025), [High-Mobility SnO Enabled by Doping-Induced Interstitial Oxygen for All-Oxide Complementary Logics](https://doi.org/10.1002/adfm.202500132).

title: Scandium segregation below the nominal phase boundary
open: Prevent nanoscale Sc-rich leakage paths while preserving switchable wurtzite AlScN. Predict precipitation from local composition fluctuations rather than average composition.
status: Sharpened by 2025 observations of metallic rocksalt precipitates and enhanced leakage even at 10% Sc.
why: Connects ferroelectric switching with predictable insulation.
key_works: D. Wu et al. (2025), [Atomic Origins of Leakage Paths in Epitaxial Al1−xScxN Thin Films](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.5c03675).

title: Coupling and acoustic loss in periodically poled AlScN
open: Increase acoustic quality factor while retaining coupling at high frequency. Quantify losses from polarity interfaces, electrodes, anchors, and intrinsic damping.
status: A 2020s challenge; 2025 four-layer resonators reached 11.8% coupling and parallel-resonance Q of 236.6 at 17.9 GHz.
why: Enables compact RF filters with lower insertion loss.
key_works: Izhar et al. (2025), [Periodically poled aluminum scandium nitride bulk acoustic wave resonators and filters for communications in the 6G era](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41378-024-00857-4).

title: Humidity-dependent selectivity of oxide chemiresistors
open: Predict hydroxyl-dependent selectivity during mixed-analyte exposure and repeated humidity changes. Transfer calibration between sensors without individually retraining humidity corrections.
status: Water interference is decades old; fluorine doping and catalytic clusters suppressed hydroxyl interference in a 2025 In₂O₃ study.
why: Enables reliable measurements outside controlled laboratory air.
key_works: Z. Jin et al. (2025), [F− dopants blocking hydroxyl interference: A facile solution for realizing humidity-resistive, selectivity adjustable, highly sensitive In2O3-based gas sensors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cej.2025.162338).

title: Long-life SnO2 sensing without morphology-driven drift
open: Stabilize sensitivity and baseline against vacancy annealing, grain coarsening, and neck growth. Demonstrate predictable multi-year sensing under thermal cycling and contaminants.
status: Drift has limited deployment for decades; Nb/Cr doping approximately halved response degradation in a 2025 study.
why: Reduces maintenance of distributed sensing networks.
key_works: A. Sagitova et al. (2025), [Restraining SnO2 gas sensor response degradation through heterovalent doping](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.snb.2025.137345).

title: Peripheral recombination versus transit time in InP DHBTs
open: Suppress peripheral recombination in submicrometre InP/GaAsSb double-heterojunction bipolar transistors while preserving transit time and low base resistance.
status: A decades-old scaling trade-off; a 2025 emitter ledge increased gain from 16 to 34 but reduced cutoff and maximum-oscillation frequencies.
why: Improves practical sub-terahertz gain and bandwidth.
key_works: Z. Liu et al. (2025), [Emitter Ledge Effect on Current Gain of Sub-Micron Type-II InP DHBT](https://csmantech.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/11B.5-Final.2025.pdf).

title: Contact resistance at vanishing silicon contact length
open: Preserve low nanosheet access resistance as contacts shrink, including current crowding, leakage, and contact lifetime.
status: A scaling problem since the 2000s; the 2024 IRDS retains worsening series-resistance penalties.
why: Preserves useful transistor drive current.
key_works: IEEE IRDS More Moore team (2024), [International Roadmap for Devices and Systems: More Moore](https://irds.ieee.org/images/files/pdf/2024/2024IRDS_MM.pdf).

title: Nanosheet gate-to-contact capacitance floor
open: Lower fringe capacitance without increasing access resistance or degrading dielectric lifetime; establish the minimum achievable energy-delay envelope.
status: Increasingly restrictive since the 2010s; the 2024 IRDS identifies coupled resistance–capacitance trade-offs.
why: Parasitics increasingly dominate switching.
key_works: IEEE IRDS More Moore team (2024), [International Roadmap for Devices and Systems: More Moore](https://irds.ieee.org/images/files/pdf/2024/2024IRDS_MM.pdf).

title: Tier-resolved self-heating in multi-tier CFETs
open: Measure individual channel temperatures during simultaneous CFET switching and validate transient thermal predictions, including effects on variability and lifetime.
status: Open since 2010s CFET development; 2026 modelling provides tier-dependent predictions requiring experimental validation.
why: Determines whether stacking increases useful throughput.
key_works: S. Shahin et al. (2026), [Self-Heating and Parasitic Effects in Multi-Tier CFET Design](https://doi.org/10.1109/JXCDC.2026.3704373).

title: Coupled ageing under nanosheet switching waveforms
open: Predict lifetime distributions when hot-carrier damage, trapping, recovery, and self-heating interact under unseen switching waveforms.
status: Individual mechanisms have decades of study; a 2024 GAA review identifies architecture-specific coupling and scaling gaps.
why: Enables realistic lifetime guardbands.
key_works: M. Wang (2024), [A Review of Reliability in Gate-All-Around Nanosheet Devices](https://doi.org/10.3390/mi15020269).

title: Independent threshold-voltage control in CFET tiers
open: Independently set complementary threshold options within tightly stacked CFETs while preserving gate integrity and circuit variation margins.
status: A 2010s–2020s problem; 2023 devices at 48-nm pitch introduced isolation enabling multi-threshold patterning.
why: Enables leakage–speed choices within stacks.
key_works: H. Mertens et al. (2023), [Nanosheet-based Complementary Field-Effect Transistors (CFETs) at 48nm Gate Pitch, and Middle Dielectric Isolation to enable CFET Inner Spacer Formation and Multi-Vt Patterning](https://doi.org/10.23919/VLSITechnologyandCir57934.2023.10185218).

title: CFET bottom-tier preservation during top-tier completion
open: Complete top-tier processing without degrading lower-tier strain, contacts, leakage, or reliability as vertical separation shrinks.
status: Open since CFET proposals; 2023 modules demonstrated 30-nm vertical n–p spacing.
why: Preserves both devices’ useful performance.
key_works: H. Mertens et al. (2023), [Nanosheet-based Complementary Field-Effect Transistors (CFETs) at 48nm Gate Pitch, and Middle Dielectric Isolation to enable CFET Inner Spacer Formation and Multi-Vt Patterning](https://doi.org/10.23919/VLSITechnologyandCir57934.2023.10185218).

title: Direct-tunnelling limit of sub-5-nm silicon logic
open: Determine which silicon geometries satisfy specified current, leakage, and voltage requirements below approximately 5-nm physical gate length. Establish lower bounds where no permitted geometry succeeds.
status: Studied since the 1990s; atomistic transport constrains possibilities without establishing a universal product-relevant boundary.
why: Separates fixable electrostatics from quantum leakage.
key_works: W. Cao et al. (2023), [The future transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06145-x).

title: Sub-10-nm low-resistance n-type contacts
open: Maintain reproducible ohmic injection through contacts shorter than 10 nm in integrated top-gated TMD transistors at logic voltages.
status: Central since the 2010s; 2025 antimony contacts reached 98 Ω·µm at 18-nm contact length and 40-nm contacted gate pitch.
why: Prevents contacts from consuming scaling benefits.
key_works: M. Du et al. (2025), [Scaled crystalline antimony ohmic contacts for two-dimensional transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-025-01500-4).

title: Low-overdrive, scaled WSe₂ pFETs
open: Combine short contacts, low hole-injection resistance, and near-thermal swing in wafer-grown WSe₂ pFETs operating below 1 V.
status: A decade-old complementarity bottleneck; 2025 devices delivered 421 µA/µm at 50-nm channel length, but the high-current condition used 2.5-V overdrive.
