why: Enables low-static-power complementary 2D circuits.
key_works: S. Ghosh et al. (2025), [High-performance p-type bilayer WSe2 field effect transistors by nitric oxide doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59684-4).

title: Subnanometre-EOT gate stacks without a reliability penalty
open: Combine subnanometre equivalent oxide thickness, low leakage, low trap density, and qualified breakdown lifetime in scalable 2D top gates.
status: Open since early TMD transistors; transferred crystalline oxides achieved 61-mV/decade swing and small hysteresis in 2024.
why: Preserves electrostatic control of atomically thin channels.
key_works: D. Zeng et al. (2024), [Single-crystalline metal-oxide dielectrics for top-gate 2D transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07786-2).

title: Electrical disorder at 2D nanoribbon edges
open: Control edge termination, vacancies, and reconstruction in approximately 5–10-nm TMD ribbons, obtaining uniform electrical behavior after complete processing.
status: Narrow-ribbon disorder has been studied since the 2000s; a 2023 integration assessment identifies stacked-ribbon edge effects as underexplored.
why: Edges can dominate otherwise excellent channels.
key_works: K. P. O’Brien et al. (2023), [Process integration and future outlook of 2D transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-41779-5).

title: Spatially selective, lifetime-stable 2D doping
open: Selectively dope source/drain extensions while preventing diffusion, remote-charge disorder, and channel contamination through processing and operation.
status: Open since the 2010s; 2026 chlorinated-solvent p-doping persisted over eight months and survived 150 °C, leaving nanoscale selectivity unresolved.
why: Enables stable low-resistance complementary extensions.
key_works: L. Hoang et al. (2026), [Low resistance p-type contacts to monolayer WSe2 through chlorinated solvent doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65604-3).

title: Chemical identification of active 2D gate traps
open: Associate active trap distributions with atomic structures and transition levels in working gates. Predict activity as channel Fermi level changes.
status: Instability has accompanied 2D FETs since the 2010s; Fermi-level tuning reduced trapping in 2022 without identifying every defect.
why: Enables targeted chemical defect control.
key_works: T. Knobloch et al. (2022), [Improving stability in two-dimensional transistors with amorphous gate oxides by Fermi-level tuning](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-022-00768-0).

title: Low-voltage 2D circuit speed beyond small oscillators
open: Demonstrate speed and energy benefits in large complementary circuits with realistic wiring, fan-out, and leakage at matched functionality and voltage.
status: Circuit integration has lagged devices since the 2010s; five-stage MoS₂ oscillators reached 2.65 GHz in 2023.
why: Establishes a useful computing technology.
key_works: D. Fan et al. (2023), [Two-dimensional semiconductor integrated circuits operating at gigahertz frequencies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01052-5).

title: Long-term 2D gate-stability extrapolation
open: Predict threshold drift by separating trapping, ionic motion, and ferroelectric effects across sweep rates, temperature, and oxide thickness.
status: Open since the 2010s; a 2025–2026 standardized hysteresis scheme shows why arbitrary hysteresis measurements cannot establish lifetime.
why: Turns short electrical tests into defensible reliability evidence.
key_works: A. Karl et al. (2026), [A standardized approach to characterize hysteresis in 2D-materials-based transistors for stability benchmarking and performance projection](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66210-z).

title: Population-level benchmark corpus for emerging FETs
open: Publish raw measurements, geometry, extraction procedures, populations, and failed devices, enabling comparisons at matched leakage, voltage, and footprint.
status: Inconsistent reporting has persisted for decades; 2022 guidelines specify requirements, but a maintained cross-laboratory corpus remains a data target.
why: Replaces champion-device comparisons with population evidence.
key_works: Z. Cheng et al. (2022), [How to report and benchmark emerging field-effect transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-022-00798-8).

title: Rare metallic nanotubes in billion-device circuits
open: Suppress and certify residual metallic-tube probabilities suitable for billion-device circuits without damaging useful tubes or losing density.
status: Open since 1990s CNT logic; highly purified aligned arrays on 10-cm wafers were demonstrated in 2020.
why: Prevents rare shorts from dominating yield.
key_works: L. Liu et al. (2020), [Aligned, high-density semiconducting carbon nanotube arrays for high-performance electronics](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aba5980).

title: CNT diameter and tube-count threshold variation
open: Bound threshold and drive-current distributions despite diameter, chirality, placement, and tube-count variation in scaled transistors.
status: Known since 1990s CNT FETs; 2020 arrays reached 100–200 tubes/µm without establishing narrow device tails.
why: Improves logic and memory yield.
key_works: L. Liu et al. (2020), [Aligned, high-density semiconducting carbon nanotube arrays for high-performance electronics](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aba5980).

title: Scaled CNT contacts for both carrier polarities
open: Retain low-resistance short contacts in complementary CNT devices after dense gate integration, with reproducible polarity and lifetime stability.
status: Open since the 2000s; a 2023 full-contact geometry reached 90 Ω·µm at 55-nm contacted gate pitch.
why: Prevents contacts from dominating ballistic-channel performance.
key_works: Y. Lin et al. (2023), [Scaling aligned carbon nanotube transistors to a sub-10 nm node](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-00983-3).

title: Long-lived complementary CNT extension doping
open: Preserve selective CNT extension doping and matched complementary thresholds through processing and prolonged bias stress at scaled dimensions.
status: Sought since the 2000s; 2023 localized solid-state doping produced thresholds of +0.29 V and −0.25 V.
why: Enables stable complementary CNT logic.
key_works: Z. Zhang et al. (2023), [Complementary carbon nanotube metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors with localized solid-state extension doping](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01047-2).

title: InGaAs interface-trap suppression across the operating band
open: Suppress bandgap-tail and conduction-band traps in InGaAs nanosheet gates, recovering swing and transconductance after aggressive dielectric scaling.
status: A decades-old III–V MOS problem; 2026 work linked nanosheet behavior to trap tails near 5 × 10¹¹ cm⁻²eV⁻¹.
why: Preserves the benefit of high channel mobility.
key_works: L. Balestra et al. (2026), [Impact of interface traps on the subthreshold performance of InGaAs nanosheet transistors](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.sse.2025.109265).

title: Microscopic mechanism of durable germanium passivation
open: Identify hydrogen configurations and reactions producing stable Ge passivation, then predict survival under bias and heat in thin gate interfaces.
status: Open through decades of Ge MOS research; a 2024 comparison finds hydrogen’s role less clear than in silicon.
why: Prevents interfaces from wasting mobility gains.
key_works: R. J. Theeuwes, W. M. M. Kessels, and B. Macco (2024), [Surface passivation approaches for silicon, germanium, and III–V semiconductors](https://doi.org/10.1116/6.0004030).

title: Tunnelling-leakage boundary for ultrascaled InGaAs
open: Identify realizable geometries and doping profiles retaining InGaAs transport benefits despite direct tunnelling, confinement, and heavier-valley occupation.
status: Investigated since the 2000s; 2015 full-band simulations showed strong sensitivity to body width and nonuniform doping.
why: Determines whether light effective mass remains advantageous.
key_works: Z. Jiang et al. (2015), [Tunneling and Short Channel Effects in Ultrascaled InGaAs Double Gate MOSFETs](https://doi.org/10.1109/TED.2014.2383392).

title: Useful-current steepness in TFETs
open: Sustain sub-60-mV/decade switching across useful currents while matching practical drive current at low voltage, including capacitance and defects.
status: Pursued since the 2000s; a 2021 integrated III–V TFET/MOSFET platform demonstrated minimum swing of 42 mV/decade.
why: Establishes circuit benefits from steep switching.
key_works: C. Convertino et al. (2021), [A hybrid III–V tunnel FET and MOSFET technology platform integrated on silicon](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-020-00531-3).

title: Matched complementary tunnel-FET logic
open: Build matched n- and p-TFETs with useful-current steepness, low ambipolar leakage, compatible processing, and cascadable noise margins.
status: A central objective since the 2000s; individual junction demonstrations leave circuit-level requirements unresolved.
why: Makes steep switches compose into logic.
key_works: A. M. Ionescu and H. Riel (2011), [Tunnel field-effect transistors as energy-efficient electronic switches](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature10679); W. Cao et al. (2023), [The future transistors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06145-x).

title: Frequency-robust negative-capacitance energy gain
open: Demonstrate net circuit-energy reduction across frequency, temperature, and variation after including ferroelectric loss and loading. Exclude transient-switching and trapping artifacts.
status: Pursued since the 2000s; 2023 work demonstrated negative differential capacitance in 1-nm hafnia and endurance exceeding 10¹⁵ cycles.
why: Tests whether voltage amplification yields system savings.
key_works: S. Jo et al. (2023), [Negative differential capacitance in ultrathin ferroelectric hafnia](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-00959-3).

title: Cold-source energy filtering after inelastic scattering
open: Preserve nonthermal source distributions through realistic contacts and channels, maintaining steepness at useful current despite phonon and carrier-mediated rethermalization.
status: Modern Dirac-source work dates to the 2010s; 2018 devices averaged 40 mV/decade over four current decades.
why: Determines whether practical carriers remain sufficiently cold.
key_works: C. Qiu et al. (2018), [Dirac-source field-effect transistors as energy-efficient, high-performance electronic switches](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aap9195).

title: Geometry-dependent speed limit of electrical Mott switching
open: Predict the complete turn-on–recovery cycle, including electronic, structural, and thermal contributions. Identify geometries supporting rapid repetition without accumulated heating.
status: Mechanisms have been debated for decades; 2026 electrical VO₂ imaging identified structural recovery as frequency-limiting.
why: Separates fast onset from useful repetition rate.
key_works: A. Pofelski et al. (2026), [Switching speed limits in electrically driven VO2 structural Mott–Peierls transition](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69904-0).

title: Retention tails in capacitorless oxide DRAM
open: Bound worst-cell retention and read-current failures in large IGZO gain-cell arrays across temperature and ageing.
status: Developed since the 2010s; 2025 vertical dual-gate cells retained data beyond 100 s in a small population.
why: Sets safe array refresh intervals.
key_works: F. Liao et al. (2025), [High-density three-dimensional integration of dynamic random-access memory using vertical dual-gate IGZO TFTs](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65925-3).

title: Predictable variable-retention-time DRAM cells
open: Predict switching between retention states and establish whether finite profiling can certify future behavior under temperature and data-pattern variation.
status: Known for decades; a 2013 study of 248 commodity chips showed why profiling misses weak states.
why: Could safely reduce refresh energy.
key_works: J. Liu et al. (2013), [An Experimental Study of Data Retention Behavior in Modern DRAM Devices: Implications for Retention Time Profiling Mechanisms](https://doi.org/10.1145/2485922.2485928).

title: Multilevel capacitorless DRAM under repeated reads
open: Preserve distinguishable gain-cell levels under read sequences, temperature changes, and unselected-line coupling after including refresh and sensing costs.
status: Active since the 2010s; 2025 IGZO cells demonstrated multibit operation in 4F² footprints.
why: Establishes usable multilevel density.
key_works: F. Liao et al. (2025), [High-density three-dimensional integration of dynamic random-access memory using vertical dual-gate IGZO TFTs](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65925-3).

title: Transferable early-retention-loss models for 3D NAND
open: Predict rapid post-programming loss across materials, layers, cycling histories, and states without refitting each condition.
status: A 2010s problem; 2018 experiments characterized early loss and proposed adaptive mitigation.
why: Preserves narrow multilevel voltage margins.
key_works: Y. Luo et al. (2018), [Improving 3D NAND Flash Memory Lifetime by Tolerating Early Retention Loss and Process Variation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05140).

title: Physical suppression of NAND retention interference
open: Suppress neighboring-state-dependent retention without sacrificing programming speed, endurance, or voltage window.
status: Neighbor interference predates 3D NAND; a distinct retention-interference mechanism was measured in 2018.
why: Reduces correlated storage errors.
key_works: Y. Luo et al. (2018), [Improving 3D NAND Flash Memory Lifetime by Tolerating Early Retention Loss and Process Variation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05140).

title: Grain-resolved random telegraph noise in NAND strings
open: Predict trap-fluctuation amplitudes and timescales from vertical-channel grain geometry, percolation, temperature, and programming history.
status: Telegraph noise is decades old; 3D channels introduced different mechanisms documented in 2017.
why: Single traps can exhaust read margins.
key_works: A. S. Spinelli, C. Monzio Compagnoni, and A. L. Lacaita (2017), [Reliability of NAND Flash Memories: Planar Cells and Emerging Issues in 3D Devices](https://doi.org/10.3390/computers6020016).

title: Multilevel NAND endurance without enlarging the voltage window
open: Increase endurance while retaining voltage window, retention, and latency by suppressing cycling-induced dielectric defects.
status: A problem since 1980s flash commercialization; 3D architectures retain high-field cycling damage.
why: Preserves dense storage state separation.
key_works: A. S. Spinelli, C. Monzio Compagnoni, and A. L. Lacaita (2017), [Reliability of NAND Flash Memories: Planar Cells and Emerging Issues in 3D Devices](https://doi.org/10.3390/computers6020016).

title: Predictive filament evolution across RRAM lifetime
open: Predict stochastic SET, RESET, and failure distributions from composition and atomic structure across cycling, coupling ion migration, heating, and electronic transport.
status: Modern oxide-RRAM research accelerated in the 2000s; filament models explain trends without general transferable lifetime prediction.
why: Reduces variability and screening costs.
key_works: D. Ielmini (2016), [Resistive switching memories based on metal oxides: mechanisms, reliability and scaling](https://doi.org/10.1088/0268-1242/31/6/063002).

title: Tenfold-lower RRAM write energy at preserved lifetime
open: Proposed target: reduce write energy tenfold against a declared fabricated baseline while preserving footprint, endurance, retention, and read margin.
status: The trade-off dates to the 2000s; 2024 SiC memristors achieved billion-cycle endurance using relatively long volt-level pulses.
why: Enables efficient frequently updated memory.
key_works: O. Kapur et al. (2024), [An ultra high-endurance memristor using back-end-of-line amorphous SiC](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-64499-2).

title: Near-unity yield of integrated hBN resistive memories
open: Control switching-enabling defects so dense arrays have predictable forming, switching, and failure distributions without excessive leakage.
status: Active since the 2010s; directly synthesized CMOS-integrated hBN memristors achieved approximately 90% yield in 2025.
why: Large arrays require much smaller failure probabilities.
key_works: J. Xie et al. (2025), [On-chip direct synthesis of boron nitride memristors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-025-01988-z).

title: Selector margins after billions of half-select stresses
open: Retain narrow threshold distributions, low leakage, and adequate drive after selected and half-selected pulses across temperature and ageing.
status: A longstanding cross-point bottleneck; 2026 selenium selectors reported 4-pA leakage, approximately 20-ns switching, and up to 2 × 10⁹ cycles.
why: Prevents sneak currents and array disturbance.
key_works: Y. Sun et al. (2026), [Charge-triggered switching mechanism in selenium selector enabling ultralow leakage current](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02499-5).

title: Symmetric open-loop RRAM conductance updates
open: Obtain small, symmetric conductance increments using fixed pulses across states, devices, temperature, and cycling without extensive verification.
status: Central since 2010s analogue computing; compensation exists, while nonlinearity and stochasticity persist.
why: Reduces learning bias and programming overhead.
key_works: D. Ielmini and H.-S. P. Wong (2018), [In-memory computing with resistive switching devices](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-018-0092-2).

title: Non-perturbing, time-resolved three-dimensional filament imaging
open: Reconstruct atomic-scale filament formation and rupture during realistic fast programming without changing the mechanism through probing or specimen preparation.
status: Imaging progressed through the 2000s; direct filament growth was observed in 2012, leaving the combined spatial, temporal, and perturbation requirement open.
why: Distinguishes models fitting similar electrical waveforms.
key_works: Y. Yang et al. (2012), [Observation of conducting filament growth in nanoscale resistive memories](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms1737).

title: Fast crystallization with long hot retention
open: Combine subnanosecond electrical crystallization with long amorphous retention at elevated temperature, including rare spontaneous-crystallization and slow-write tails.
status: A longstanding trade-off; scandium–antimony–tellurium enabled 700-ps writing in 2017.
why: Enables fast nonvolatile storage.
key_works: F. Rao et al. (2017), [Reducing the stochasticity of crystal nucleation to enable subnanosecond memory writing](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aao3212).

title: Composition-predictive phase-change resistance ageing
open: Predict resistance ageing from amorphous motifs across compositions and thermal histories, including which relaxation events leave resistance unchanged.
status: Studied since the 2000s; practically drift-free CrTe₃ was reported in 2025–2026.
why: Replaces empirical alloy searches.
key_works: X. Wang et al. (2025 online; 2026 issue), [Amorphous phase-change memory alloy with no resistance drift](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-025-02361-0).

title: Tenfold reduction of electrically reset PCM energy
open: Proposed target: lower RESET energy tenfold against a declared scaled baseline, preserving speed, retention, read margin, and endurance, including contact losses.
status: Thermal-confinement research spans decades; 2024 superlattice devices demonstrated approximately 0.7-V switching at 40-nm dimensions.
why: Reduces melt–quench energy costs.
key_works: X. Wu et al. (2024), [Novel nanocomposite-superlattices for low energy and high stability nanoscale phase-change memory](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42792-4).

title: Suppression of PCM composition segregation during cycling
open: Prevent segregation and void formation from changing active volume during repeated melting and quenching. Predict failure tails under variable pulses and multilevel programming.
status: Decades old; 2025 nano-confined cells exceeded 1.1 × 10¹¹ cycles and linked carbon segregation to failure.
why: Stabilizes switching parameters and lifetime.
key_works: J. Zheng et al. (2025), [Extended switching endurance of phase change memory through nano-confined cell structure](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60644-1).

title: Electrically programmed drift-free multilevel PCM arrays
open: Transfer low-drift materials into dense electrical multilevel arrays with useful speed, noise margins, and cycling life.
status: Pursued since the 2000s; CrTe₃ established near-zero amorphous drift and hybrid optoelectronic multilevel encoding in 2025–2026.
why: Enables dependable analogue storage.
key_works: X. Wang et al. (2025 online; 2026 issue), [Amorphous phase-change memory alloy with no resistance drift](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-025-02361-0).

title: Ultimate stable bit volume in hafnia ferroelectrics
open: Determine minimum bit area and thickness supporting distinguishable states with useful retention, including depolarization, phase competition, boundaries, and leakage.
status: Hafnia ferroelectricity emerged in 2011; switchable polarization at 1-nm thickness was demonstrated on silicon in 2020.
why: Establishes polarization-storage density limits.
key_works: S. S. Cheema et al. (2020), [Enhanced ferroelectricity in ultrathin films grown directly on silicon](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2208-x).

title: CMOS-compatible hafnia fatigue suppression
open: Reproduce extreme cycling endurance together with retention in scaled silicon-compatible stacks, preserving defect control within acceptable processing temperatures.
status: Central since 2011; 2025 structures exceeded 10¹² cycles but used integration-demanding thermal budgets and oxide electrodes.
why: Translates capacitor records into manufacturable memories.
key_works: C. Zhou et al. (2025), [Fatigue-free ferroelectricity in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ultrathin films via interfacial design](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63048-3).

title: FeFET polarization–charge-trapping disentanglement
open: Separate polarization and trapped-charge contributions during programming, retention, and ageing; predict when increased memory window conceals damage.
status: Decades old, renewed by hafnia after 2011; a 2020 assessment identifies coupled reliability challenges.
why: Makes memory-window interpretation trustworthy.
key_works: A. I. Khan, A. Keshavarzi, and S. Datta (2020), [The future of ferroelectric field-effect transistor technology](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-020-00492-7).

title: Low-voltage ferroelectric tunnel-junction margins
open: Combine large persistent electroresistance, low-voltage writing, endurance, and small-area uniformity in the same operating regime.
status: Explored since the 2000s; 2024 junctions achieved 1-nm barriers and billions of cycles, with contrast and endurance optimized under different pulses.
why: Makes extreme resistance ratios practically usable.
key_works: Y. Jia et al. (2024), [Giant tunnelling electroresistance in atomic-scale ferroelectric tunnel junctions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-44927-7).

title: Scaled FeFET multilevel domain reproducibility
open: Set stable intermediate states with few grains or domains, bounding switching noise, retention spread, and read disturbance without costly verification.
status: Multilevel concepts predate hafnia; miniaturization removes averaging available in larger gates.
why: Preserves analogue density benefits.
key_works: A. I. Khan, A. Keshavarzi, and S. Datta (2020), [The future of ferroelectric field-effect transistor technology](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-020-00492-7).

title: Low-current STT switching at retained thermal stability
open: Reduce current for fast, low-error switching while retaining thermal stability and tunnel-barrier lifetime across temperature and manufacturing variation.
status: A central trade-off since the 1990s; 2025 ferrimagnetic Heusler junctions demonstrated nanosecond switching at 10⁻⁷ write-error rate.
why: Reduces MRAM cell area and write energy.
key_works: C. Garg et al. (2025), [Ferrimagnetic Heusler tunnel junctions with fast spin-transfer torque switching enabled by low magnetization](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-024-01827-7).

title: Field-free SOT array error tails
open: Retain deterministic field-free switching in dense arrays with short pulses, low current, and bounded errors across variation and thermal processing.
status: Pursued since the 2010s; 2024 ferromagnetic trilayers demonstrated field-free subnanosecond switching.
why: Removes cell-specific optimization from manufacturing.
key_works: Q. Yang et al. (2024), [Field-free spin–orbit torque switching in ferromagnetic trilayers at sub-ns timescales](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46113-1).

title: Robust voltage-controlled magnetic-anisotropy writing
open: Achieve voltage-driven switching with timing-tolerant pulses, retention, and barrier lifetime, reducing dependence on precise precession timing or auxiliary fields.
status: Investigated since the 2000s; a 2024 assessment retains unresolved practical VCMA trade-offs.
why: Could reduce magnetic-memory write dissipation.
key_works: D. C. Worledge and G. Hu (2024), [Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory technology status and future directions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44287-024-00111-z).

title: Unambiguous low-energy antiferromagnetic memory states
open: Electrically write and distinguish stable antiferromagnetic states while excluding thermal, strain, and irreversible structural artifacts. Establish energy, retention, endurance, and read margin together.
status: CuMnAs electrical switching was demonstrated in 2016; scalable low-energy readout remains a stronger requirement.
why: Makes low-stray-field magnetic storage practical.
key_works: P. Wadley et al. (2016), [Electrical switching of an antiferromagnet](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aab1031).

title: Error-bounded skyrmion racetrack displacement
open: Reproducibly create, move, stop, and delete skyrmions in imperfect tracks, with error models including interactions, temperature, and pulse variation.
status: A 2010s racetrack objective; 2024 calculations found residual Hall deflection and trapping even for antiferromagnetic skyrmions.
why: Establishes reliable bit positioning and survival.
key_works: A. Aldarawsheh et al. (2024), [Current-driven dynamics of antiferromagnetic skyrmions: from skyrmion Hall effects to hybrid inter-skyrmion scattering](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44306-024-00049-w).

title: Conversion-inclusive energy advantage of analogue arrays
subfield: Analogue in-memory computing devices and arrays
open: Preserve analogue arithmetic advantages after including conversion, drivers, activations, and communication at matched workload accuracy and latency.
status: Studied since the 2010s; a 2023 64-core PCM chip integrated digital functions and showed precision-dependent efficiency.
why: Prevents peripherals from consuming arithmetic savings.
key_works: M. Le Gallo et al. (2023), [A 64-core mixed-signal in-memory compute chip based on phase-change memory for deep neural network inference](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01010-1).

title: Tenfold system-energy gain for autoregressive analogue inference
subfield: Analogue in-memory computing devices and arrays
open: Proposed target: reduce energy per generated token tenfold against matched digital hardware, including loading, nonlinear operations, and memory traffic at equal quality and latency.
status: Active since the 2010s; 2023 analogue hardware demonstrated multi-chip speech inference with 45 million weights.
why: Addresses utilization and movement costs in token generation.
key_works: S. Ambrogio et al. (2023), [An analog-AI chip for energy-efficient speech recognition and transcription](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06337-5).

title: Large-model in-situ training without precision rescue costs
subfield: Analogue in-memory computing devices and arrays
open: Train large networks through physical conductance updates with software-quality convergence and net energy savings, including correction, drift, asymmetry, and finite endurance.
status: Active since the 2010s; 2018 hybrid PCM/capacitor training achieved equivalent accuracy using compensation and mixed storage.
why: Prevents digital correction from erasing update savings.
key_works: S. Ambrogio et al. (2018), [Equivalent-accuracy accelerated neural-network training using analogue memory](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0180-5).

title: Fast electrochemical RAM with persistent analogue states
subfield: Analogue in-memory computing devices and arrays
open: Combine rapid symmetric updates, long retention, low read disturbance, and small footprint by controlling ionic leakage without slowing writes.
status: ECRAM expanded in the 2010s; 2023 CMOS-compatible arrays demonstrated approximately megahertz programming, 150 × 150-nm² devices, and over 10⁸ cycles.
why: Reconciles fast ion movement with stable storage.
key_works: J. Cui et al. (2023), [CMOS-compatible electrochemical synaptic transistor arrays for deep learning accelerators](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-00939-7).
